title.zh: 卷75 尒朱兆 尒朱彦伯 尒朱度律 尒朱天光
title.en: Volume 75: Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Yanbo, Erzhu Dulu, Erzhu Tianguang
title.raw: 卷75 尒朱兆 尒朱彦伯 尒朱度律 尒朱天光 Volume 75: Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Yanbo, Erzhu Dulu, Erzhu Tianguang

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆 尒朱彥伯 尒朱度律 尒朱天光

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Yanbo, Erzhu Dulu, Erzhu Tianguang
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Yanbo, Erzhu Dulu, and Erzhu Tianguang

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆，字萬仁，榮從子也。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao, style name Wanren, was Rong's nephew by the collateral line.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, whose style name was Wanren, was a nephew of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 少驍猛，善騎射，手格猛獸，蹻捷過人。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and bold, skilled at mounted archery, grappling fierce beasts with his hands, and more nimble than others.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was fierce and bold, expert at mounted archery, able to grapple fierce beasts with his bare hands, and swifter and more agile than anyone around him.

sentences.zh: 數從榮遊獵，至於窮巖絕澗人所不能升降者，兆先之。

translations.literal: He often followed Rong on hunting excursions; when they came to sheer cliffs and sheer ravines where people could not ascend or descend, Zhao went ahead first.
translations.idiomatic: He often accompanied Rong on the hunt, and whenever they reached sheer cliffs and impassable ravines that others could not climb, Zhao would go first.

sentences.zh: 榮以此特加賞愛，任為爪牙。

translations.literal: Because of this Rong especially prized and favored him, and appointed him as his claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong prized him all the more for this and made him one of his trusted enforcers.

sentences.zh: 榮曾送臺使，見二鹿，乃命兆前，止授二箭，曰：「可取此鹿供今食也。」

translations.literal: Once when Rong was escorting an envoy from the capital he saw two deer, and ordered Zhao forward, giving him only two arrows, saying: "You may take these deer to supply today's meal."
translations.idiomatic: Once, while escorting an envoy from the capital, Rong spotted two deer and sent Zhao ahead with only two arrows, saying, "Bring back these deer for today's meal."

sentences.zh: 遂停馬構火以待之。

translations.literal: He then halted his horse, built a fire, and waited for him.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismounted, kindled a fire, and waited.

sentences.zh: 俄然兆獲其一。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao obtained one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao returned with one of the deer.

sentences.zh: 榮欲矜夸，使人責兆曰：「何不盡取？」

translations.literal: Rong wished to show off and had someone reproach Zhao, saying: "Why did you not take them all?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to put on a show of authority and sent someone to rebuke Zhao: "Why did you not bring back both?"

sentences.zh: 杖之五十。

translations.literal: He had him beaten fifty strokes with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Zhao beaten fifty strokes with the staff.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功除平遠將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 榮之入洛，兆兼前鋒都督。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Zhao concurrently served as commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong marched into Luoyang, Zhao served concurrently as commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊即阼，特除中軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫，又假驍騎將軍、建興太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, he was specially appointed General of the Central Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and was also given acting rank as General of Valiant Cavalry and Administrator of Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Zhao was specially appointed General of the Central Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and was also given acting rank as General of Valiant Cavalry and Administrator of Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節、車騎將軍、武衞將軍、左光祿大夫、都督、潁川郡開國公，食邑千二百戶。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, General of Martial Guards, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Commander-in-Chief, and Duke of Yingchuan Commandery with a fief of twelve hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he received the staff of authority as General of Chariots and Cavalry and General of Martial Guards, was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and commander-in-chief, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan Commandery with a fief of twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後從上黨王天穆討平邢杲。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Prince of Shangdang, Tianmu, in suppressing and pacifying Xing Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Tianmu, Prince of Shangdang, in the campaign that put down Xing Guo.

sentences.zh: 及元顥之屯於河橋，榮遣兆與賀拔勝等自馬渚西夜渡數百騎，襲擊顥子冠受，擒之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao was encamped at Heqiao, Rong sent Zhao with Helaba Sheng and others to cross by night from the west of Mazhu with several hundred horsemen, make a surprise attack on Hao's son Guanshou, and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao was encamped at Heqiao, Rong sent Zhao with Helaba Sheng and others to ford the river west of Mazhu by night with several hundred horsemen, surprise Yuan Hao's son Guanshou, and take him captive.

sentences.zh: 又進破安豐王延明，顥於是退走。

translations.literal: He then advanced and defeated the Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, and Hao thereupon withdrew in flight.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced and defeated the Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, and Yuan Hao withdrew in defeat.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，論功除散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, his merit was assessed and he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Chief of the Three Excellencies of Honor, with his fief increased by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Zhao was rewarded with appointment as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Chief of the Three Excellencies of Honor, and his fief was increased by eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 為汾州刺史，復增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He became Governor of Fen Province and his fief was again increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor of Fen Province, and his fief was increased by another thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中、驃騎大將軍，又增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was additionally made Palace Attendant and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and his fief was again increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Palace Attendant and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and his fief grew by five hundred households more.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱榮死也，兆自汾州率騎據晉陽。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Zhao led horsemen from Fen Province and seized Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Zhao led his cavalry from Fen Province and seized Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 元曄立，[1]授兆大將軍，爵為王。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, [1] Zhao was appointed Grand General and ennobled as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, [1] Zhao was appointed Grand General and ennobled as a prince.

sentences.zh: 兆與世隆等定謀攻洛，兆遂率眾南出。

translations.literal: Zhao with Shilong and others settled on a plan to attack Luoyang, and Zhao thereupon led his forces south.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Shilong and the others agreed on a plan to attack Luoyang, and Zhao led his army south.

sentences.zh: 進達太行，大都督源子恭下都督史仵龍開壘降兆，子恭退走。

translations.literal: Advancing to the Taihang range, under the Great Commander-in-Chief Yuan Zigong, the commander under him, the Registrar Wu Long, opened the fortress and surrendered to Zhao, and Zigong withdrew in flight.
translations.idiomatic: As he advanced to the Taihang Mountains, Wu Long, a commander under the Great Commander-in-Chief Yuan Zigong, opened the fortress and surrendered to Zhao, and Zigong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 兆輕兵倍道從河梁西涉渡，掩襲京邑。

translations.literal: Zhao with light troops traveled by double marches, forded the crossing west of Heqiao, and made a surprise attack on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao marched his light troops at forced pace, forded the river west of Heqiao, and launched a surprise attack on the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，河邊人夢神謂己曰：「尒朱家欲渡河，用爾作灅波津令，為之縮水脉。」

translations.literal: Earlier, a man by the river dreamed that a god said to him: "The Erzhu family wishes to cross the river; I will use you as magistrate of Zhanbo Ford to shrink the water's pulse for them."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man living by the river had dreamed that a god told him, "The Erzhu clan means to cross the river. I will make you magistrate of Zhanbo Ford and have you shrink the current for them."

sentences.zh: 月餘，夢者死。

translations.literal: After more than a month the dreamer died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later the dreamer died.

sentences.zh: 及兆至，有行人自言知水淺處，以草往往表插而導道焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao arrived, a traveler of his own accord said he knew where the water was shallow, and marked the way by sticking grass here and there as guides.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao arrived, a passerby volunteered that he knew where the water was shallow and marked the ford by sticking tufts of grass along the route.

sentences.zh: 忽失其所在。

translations.literal: Suddenly he vanished from where he had been.
translations.idiomatic: Then he vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 兆遂策馬涉渡。

translations.literal: Zhao thereupon spurred his horse and forded across.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao spurred his horse across the ford.

sentences.zh: 是日，暴風鼓怒，黃塵漲天，騎叩宮門，宿衞乃覺。

translations.literal: That day a violent wind raged, yellow dust filled the sky, and when the horsemen knocked on the palace gates the night guards only then became aware.
translations.idiomatic: That day a violent wind rose and yellow dust blotted out the sky. The horsemen were at the palace gates before the night guards even realized what was happening.

sentences.zh: 彎弓欲射，袍撥弦，矢不得發，一時散走。

translations.literal: They bent their bows intending to shoot, but their robes caught the bowstrings and the arrows could not be loosed; in an instant they scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They strung their bows to shoot, but their robes caught the strings and the arrows would not fly; in an instant they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝步出雲龍門外，為兆騎所縶，幽於永寧佛寺。

translations.literal: The emperor walked out beyond the Gate of Cloud Dragon, was seized by Zhao's horsemen, and was confined in the Yongning Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor walked out beyond the Gate of Cloud Dragon, was seized by Zhao's horsemen, and confined in Yongning Monastery.

sentences.zh: 兆撲殺皇子，汙辱妃嬪，縱兵虜掠。

translations.literal: Zhao beat to death the imperial princes, violated and shamed the consorts and concubines, and let his soldiers plunder and carry off booty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had the imperial princes beaten to death, violated the palace women, and let his troops loot at will.

sentences.zh: 停洛旬餘，先令衞送莊帝於晉陽。

translations.literal: He remained in Luoyang for more than ten days, and first had guards escort Emperor Zhuang to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He lingered in Luoyang for more than ten days, first sending guards to escort Emperor Zhuang to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 兆後於河梁監閱財貨，遂害帝於三級寺。

translations.literal: Zhao later at Heqiao supervised and inspected the goods and wealth, and then killed the emperor at the Three-Tier Monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao later went to Heqiao to oversee the seized goods and there murdered the emperor at the Three-Tier Monastery.

translations.literal: Editorial note 2.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note 2.

sentences.zh: 初，兆將向洛也，遣使招齊獻武王，欲與同舉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhao was about to march on Luoyang, he sent an envoy to summon the Prince of Qi, Xianwu, wishing to rise together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Zhao was preparing to march on Luoyang, he sent an envoy to summon Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu, hoping to raise the standard together with him.

sentences.zh: 王時為晉州刺史，謂長史孫騰曰：「臣而伐君，其逆已甚。

translations.literal: The prince was then Governor of Jin Province and said to his Chief Clerk Sun Teng: "For a subject to attack his ruler—the rebellion is already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was then Governor of Jin Province. He told his chief clerk Sun Teng, "For a subject to attack his sovereign is the gravest of rebellions.

sentences.zh: 我今不往，彼必致恨。

translations.literal: If I do not go now, he will surely bear resentment.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not go now, he is sure to bear a grudge.

sentences.zh: 卿可往申吾意，但云山蜀未平，今方攻討，不可委之而去，致有後憂。

translations.literal: You may go and convey my intent, only saying that the mountains of Shu are not yet pacified and that we are now in the midst of attack and suppression, and that I cannot abandon this and depart, lest there be later troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Go and explain my position: say only that Shu is not yet pacified, that I am in the middle of a campaign, and that I cannot leave my post and invite trouble later.

sentences.zh: 定蜀之日，當隔河為犄角之勢。

translations.literal: On the day Shu is settled, I shall form a pincer position across the river with him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu is settled, I will take up a pincer position with him across the river.

sentences.zh: 如此報之，以觀其趣。」

translations.literal: Report to him in this way to observe his inclination."
translations.idiomatic: Report to him in those terms and see how he reacts."

sentences.zh: 騰乃詣兆，及之於并州大谷，具申王言。

translations.literal: Teng then went to Zhao and overtook him at the Great Valley of Bing Province, fully conveying the prince's words.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng went to Zhao and caught up with him at the Great Valley in Bing Province, relaying Gao Huan's message in full.

sentences.zh: 兆殊不悅，且曰：「還白高兄，弟有吉夢，今段之行必有克獲。」

translations.literal: Zhao was extremely displeased and moreover said: "Return and tell Elder Brother Gao: your younger brother had an auspicious dream; on this present expedition there will surely be capture and gain."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was deeply displeased and said, "Go back and tell Elder Brother Gao: I have had an auspicious dream, and this campaign is sure to succeed."

sentences.zh: 騰問：「王夢如何？」

translations.literal: Teng asked: "What was the prince's dream?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng asked, "What was your dream?"

sentences.zh: 兆答曰：「吾比夢吾亡父登一高堆，堆旁之地悉皆耕熟，唯有馬藺草株往往猶在。

translations.literal: Zhao answered: "Recently I dreamed that my deceased father ascended a high mound; the land beside the mound was all thoroughly plowed and ripe, and only clumps of iris here and there still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao answered, "I dreamed that my dead father climbed a high mound. The ground around it was all plowed and ripe, but clumps of iris still stood here and there.

sentences.zh: 吾父問言何故不拔，左右云堅不可去。

translations.literal: My father asked why they were not pulled up; those at his side said they were firm and could not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: My father asked why they had not been pulled up. Those beside him said the roots were too firm to remove.

sentences.zh: 吾父顧我令下拔之，吾手所至，無不盡出。

translations.literal: My father turned to me and ordered me to go down and pull them up; wherever my hand reached, none failed to come out completely.
translations.idiomatic: My father turned to me and told me to pull them up myself. Wherever my hand reached, every root came clean out of the ground.

sentences.zh: 以此而言，往必有利。」

translations.literal: Judging by this, if I go there will surely be advantage."
translations.idiomatic: By that omen, the campaign is bound to succeed."

sentences.zh: 騰還具報，王曰：「兆等猖狂，舉兵犯上，吾今不同，猜忌成矣，勢不可反事尒朱。

translations.literal: Teng returned and reported in full; the prince said: "Zhao and the others are wildly arrogant, raising troops to violate their superiors; if I do not join them now, suspicion is already formed, and the situation makes it impossible to turn back and serve the Erzhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Teng reported back in full, Gao Huan said, "Zhao and his faction are out of control, raising arms against the throne. If I do not join them now, suspicion is already fixed, and I can no longer turn back and serve the Erzhu.

sentences.zh: 今也南行，天子列兵河上，兆進不能渡，退不得還。

translations.literal: Now if I march south, the Son of Heaven will array troops on the river; Zhao advancing cannot cross, and retreating cannot return.
translations.idiomatic: If I march south now, the emperor will array troops along the river. Zhao will not be able to advance across it, and he will not be able to retreat.

sentences.zh: 吾乘山東下，出其不意，此徒可以一舉而擒。」

translations.literal: I shall ride the mountains down east, take them unawares, and this band can be captured in a single stroke."
translations.idiomatic: I will come down from the mountains to the east and take them by surprise. We can seize the whole lot in one stroke."

sentences.zh: 俄而，兆克京師，孝莊幽縶。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao captured the capital, and Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao took the capital, and Emperor Xiaozhuang was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 都督尉景從兆南行，以書報王。

translations.literal: The commander Yu Jing followed Zhao south and reported to the prince by letter.
translations.idiomatic: The commander Yu Jing marched south with Zhao and sent Gao Huan a letter with the news.

sentences.zh: 王得書大驚，召騰示之曰：「卿可馳驛詣兆，示以謁賀，密觀天子今在何處，為隨兆軍府，為別送晉陽。

translations.literal: The prince, receiving the letter, was greatly alarmed; he summoned Teng, showed it to him, and said: "You may ride post-haste to Zhao, present congratulations on paying respects, and secretly observe where the Son of Heaven is now—whether he follows Zhao's army headquarters or is separately sent to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was greatly alarmed when he read the letter. He summoned Sun Teng and said, "Ride post-haste to Zhao. Offer formal congratulations, but find out in secret where the emperor is—whether he is with Zhao's headquarters or being sent separately to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 脫其送并，卿宜馳報，吾當於路邀迎，唱大義於天下。」

translations.literal: If he is sent to Bing, you should ride and report at once; I shall intercept and welcome him on the road and proclaim the great cause to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: If they are sending him to Bing Province, report back at once. I will intercept him on the road and proclaim the righteous cause to the realm."

sentences.zh: 騰晨夜驅馳，已遇帝於中路。

translations.literal: Teng drove day and night, and had already encountered the emperor on the middle of the road.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng rode day and night, but met the emperor already on the road.

sentences.zh: 王時率騎東轉，聞帝已渡，於是西還。

translations.literal: The prince was then leading horsemen in an eastward turn; hearing that the emperor had already crossed, he thereupon returned west.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had been leading his cavalry eastward, but when he heard the emperor had already been taken across the river, he turned back west.

sentences.zh: 仍與兆書，陳其福禍，不宜害天子，受惡名。

translations.literal: He then wrote to Zhao, setting forth fortune and misfortune, that he should not harm the Son of Heaven and incur an evil name.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote again to Zhao, laying out the consequences and urging him not to harm the emperor and earn an infamous name.

sentences.zh: 兆怒不納，帝遂暴崩。

translations.literal: Zhao in anger would not accept it, and the emperor thereupon died a sudden death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao refused in anger, and the emperor was murdered.

sentences.zh: 初，榮既死，莊帝詔河西人紇豆陵步蕃等令襲秀容。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Rong had died, Emperor Zhuang issued an edict to the Hexi man Yidouling Bufan and others ordering them to strike at Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Rong's death, Emperor Zhuang had ordered the Hexi commander Yidouling Bufan and others to strike at Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 兆入洛後，步蕃兵勢甚盛，南逼晉陽，兆所以不暇留洛，回師禦之。

translations.literal: After Zhao entered Luoyang, Bufan's military strength was very powerful, pressing south on Jinyang; this is why Zhao had no leisure to remain in Luoyang and turned his army to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao entered Luoyang, Bufan's forces grew very strong and pressed south toward Jinyang, which is why Zhao could not linger in the capital and had to turn back to face him.

sentences.zh: 兆雖驍果，本無策略，頻為步蕃所敗，於是部勒士馬，謀出山東。

translations.literal: Although Zhao was fierce and resolute, he fundamentally had no strategy, and was repeatedly defeated by Bufan; he thereupon marshaled soldiers and horses and planned to go out to the east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was bold in battle but had no real strategy, and Bufan defeated him again and again. He then regrouped his forces and planned to march east of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 令人頻徵獻武王於晉州，乃分三州六鎮之人，令王統領。

translations.literal: He had people repeatedly summon the Prince of Qi, Xianwu, to Jin Province, and then divided out the people of the three provinces and six garrisons and had the prince command them.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly summoned Gao Huan to Jin Province and placed the populations of three provinces and six garrisons under his command.

sentences.zh: 既分兵別營，乃引兵南出，以避步蕃之銳。

translations.literal: Having divided the troops into separate camps, he then led his army south to avoid Bufan's sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had split his forces into separate camps, he marched south to avoid Bufan's main strength.

sentences.zh: 步蕃至於樂平郡，王與兆還討破之，斬步蕃於秀容之石鼓山，其眾退走。

translations.literal: When Bufan reached Leping Commandery, the prince and Zhao returned to attack and defeat him, beheaded Bufan at Stone Drum Mountain in Xiurong, and his masses withdrew in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When Bufan reached Leping Commandery, Gao Huan and Zhao turned back, defeated him, and beheaded him at Stone Drum Mountain in Xiurong. His army fled.

sentences.zh: 兆將數十騎詣王，通夜宴飲。

translations.literal: Zhao led several tens of horsemen to visit the prince and feasted and drank with him through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao came to Gao Huan with a few dozen horsemen, and they feasted together through the night.

sentences.zh: 後還營招王，王知兆難信，未能顯示，將欲詣之。

translations.literal: Later he returned to camp and summoned the prince; the prince knew Zhao was hard to trust but could not show it openly, and was about to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao returned to camp and summoned Gao Huan again. Gao Huan knew Zhao could not be trusted but could not show it openly, and was about to go to him.

sentences.zh: 臨上馬，長史孫騰牽衣而止。

translations.literal: As he was about to mount his horse, the Chief Clerk Sun Teng seized his garment and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to mount, Sun Teng seized his robe and held him back.

sentences.zh: 兆乃隔水責罵騰等。

translations.literal: Zhao then, across the water, reproached and reviled Teng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao shouted abuse at Sun Teng and the others from across the water.

sentences.zh: 於是各去，王還自襄垣東出，兆歸晉陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon each departed; the prince returned, setting out east from Xiangyuan, and Zhao went back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: They parted: Gao Huan marched east from Xiangyuan, and Zhao returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 及前廢帝立，授兆使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、柱國大將軍、領軍將軍、領左右、并州刺史、兼錄尚書事、大行臺。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor was enthroned, Zhao was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad, Grand General of the State Pillar, Commander of the Army, Commander of the Left and Right, Governor of Bing Province, and concurrently Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner of the Great Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor was enthroned, Zhao was given the staff of authority as Palace Attendant, commander-in-chief of all military affairs at home and abroad, Grand General of the State Pillar, commander of the army and of the left and right guards, Governor of Bing Province, and concurrently Recorder of the Masters of Writing and head of the Grand Office.

sentences.zh: 又以兆為天柱大將軍，兆謂人曰：「此是叔父終官，我何敢受。」

translations.literal: He also made Zhao Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar; Zhao said to people: "This was my uncle's final office—how dare I accept it."
translations.idiomatic: He also offered Zhao the title Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar. Zhao said, "That was my uncle's final rank. How dare I accept it."

sentences.zh: 遂固辭不拜。

translations.literal: He thereupon firmly declined and would not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋加都督十州諸軍事，世襲并州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of Ten Provinces, with hereditary succession as Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made commander-in-chief of military affairs in ten provinces, with the governorship of Bing Province made hereditary in his line.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王之克殷州也，兆與仲遠、度律約共討之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi, Xianwu, captured Yin Province, Zhao with Zhongyuan and Dulu agreed together to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu, captured Yin Province, Zhao agreed with Zhongyuan and Dulu to join forces against him.

sentences.zh: 仲遠、度律次於陽平，兆出井陘，屯於廣阿，眾號十萬。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and Dulu encamped at Yangping; Zhao came out through Jingxing Pass and encamped at Guang'a, his forces numbering a hundred thousand by report.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and Dulu encamped at Yangping. Zhao came through Jingxing Pass and encamped at Guang'a with a reported force of one hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 王廣縱反間，或云世隆兄弟謀欲害兆，復言兆與王同圖仲遠等，於是兩不相信，各致猜疑，徘徊不進。

translations.literal: The prince widely spread counter-intelligence: some said Shilong and his brothers plotted to harm Zhao; others said Zhao and the prince together plotted against Zhongyuan and the others; thereupon the two sides did not trust each other, each bred suspicion, and they lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan spread disinformation far and wide: some reports said Shilong and his brothers meant to kill Zhao; others said Zhao and Gao Huan were plotting against Zhongyuan and the rest. Trust collapsed on both sides, suspicion grew, and the armies stalled.

sentences.zh: 仲遠等頻使斛斯椿、賀拔勝往喻之，兆輕騎三百來就仲遠，同坐幕下。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and the others repeatedly sent Husijun and Helaba Sheng to explain matters to him; Zhao came with three hundred light horsemen to join Zhongyuan and sat together beneath the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and the others repeatedly sent Husijun and Helaba Sheng to reason with Zhao. Zhao came to Zhongyuan's camp with three hundred light horsemen and sat with him beneath the tent.

sentences.zh: 兆性粗獷，意色不平，手舞馬鞭，長嘯凝望，深疑仲遠等有變，遂趨出馳還。

translations.literal: Zhao's nature was coarse and fierce; his expression and color were not calm; he waved a horsewhip in his hand, gave a long whistle and gazed fixedly, deeply suspecting that Zhongyuan and the others had treachery in mind, and thereupon rushed out and galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was coarse and volatile. His face darkened, he whipped his horsewhip through the air, gave a long whistle, and stared hard, deeply suspecting treachery from Zhongyuan and the others. He bolted from the tent and galloped back to his camp.

sentences.zh: 仲遠遣椿、勝等追而曉譬，兆遂拘縛將還，經日放遣。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan sent Chun, Sheng, and others in pursuit to explain and enlighten him; Zhao thereupon bound and seized them intending to take them back, and after a day released them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan sent Chun, Sheng, and the others after him to explain. Zhao seized and bound them, intending to take them back with him, but released them after a day.

sentences.zh: 仲遠等於是奔退。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan and the others thereupon fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan and his allies then broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 王乃進擊兆，兆軍大敗。

translations.literal: The prince then advanced to attack Zhao, and Zhao's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then attacked Zhao, and Zhao's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 兆與仲遠、度律遂相疑阻，久而不和。

translations.literal: Zhao with Zhongyuan and Dulu thereupon mutually suspected and obstructed one another, and for a long time were not reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, Zhongyuan, and Dulu grew mutually suspicious and remained at odds for a long time.

sentences.zh: 世隆請前廢帝納兆女為后，兆乃大喜。

translations.literal: Shilong requested that the Former Deposed Emperor take Zhao's daughter as empress, and Zhao thereupon was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong persuaded the Former Deposed Emperor to take Zhao's daughter as empress, and Zhao was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 世隆厚禮喻兆赴洛，深示卑下，隨其所為，無敢違者。

translations.literal: Shilong with generous gifts persuaded Zhao to go to Luoyang, showing deep humility and deference; whatever he wished, none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong courted Zhao with lavish gifts and urged him to come to Luoyang, showing the deepest deference. Whatever Zhao wanted, no one dared refuse.

sentences.zh: 兆與天光、度律更自信約，然後大會於韓陵山。

translations.literal: Zhao with Tianguang and Dulu renewed their pledge of trust, and then held a great assembly at Hanling Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao renewed his pact with Tianguang and Dulu, and then the allies gathered in force at Hanling Mountain.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，復奔晉陽，遂大掠并州城內。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, he again fled to Jinyang and thereupon carried out great plunder within Bing Province's city.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in battle, he fled again to Jinyang and looted the city of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 獻武王自鄴進討之，兆遂走於秀容。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Xianwu, advanced from Ye to campaign against him, and Zhao thereupon fled to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan advanced from Ye to pursue him, and Zhao fled to Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 王又追擊，度赤洪嶺，破之，眾並降散。

translations.literal: The prince again pursued in attack, crossed Red Flood Ridge, defeated him, and his masses all surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan pursued him again, crossed Red Flood Ridge, broke his force, and his men surrendered or scattered.

sentences.zh: 兆竄於窮山，殺所乘馬，自縊於樹。

translations.literal: Zhao fled into a remote mountain, killed the horse he was riding, and hanged himself from a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fled into the wild hills, killed his horse, and hanged himself from a tree.

sentences.zh: 王收而葬之。

translations.literal: The prince recovered his body and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan recovered the body and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 兆果於戰鬬，每有征伐，常居鋒首，當時諸將伏其材力。

translations.literal: Zhao was resolute in battle; whenever there was a campaign he constantly held the forefront, and the generals of the time submitted to his talent and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was fierce in battle and always took the lead in every campaign; the generals of the day respected his strength.

sentences.zh: 而粗脫少智，無將領之能。

translations.literal: Yet he was coarse, unrestrained, and lacking in wisdom, without the ability of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: But he was crude, rash, and not very clever, and lacked the talents of a true commander.

sentences.zh: 榮雖奇其膽決，然每云「兆不過將三千騎，多則亂矣」。

translations.literal: Although Rong marveled at his boldness and resolution, he would always say: "Zhao is fit to command no more than three thousand horsemen; with more he falls into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Rong admired his boldness, yet he often said, "Zhao is good for no more than three thousand horsemen. Give him more and he falls apart."

sentences.zh: 兆弟智虎，前廢帝封為安定王，驃騎大將軍、肆州刺史、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Zhihu was enfeoffed by the Former Deposed Emperor as Prince of Anding, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Si Province, and Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Zhihu was enfeoffed by the Former Deposed Emperor as Prince of Anding, with the ranks of Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Si Province, and Grandee of the First Order with an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 與兆俱走，獻武王擒之於梁郡岢嵐南山，赦之。

translations.literal: He fled together with Zhao; the Prince of Qi, Xianwu, captured him at the Southern Mountain of Kelan in Liang Commandery and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He fled with Zhao, but Gao Huan captured him on the southern slope of Kelan in Liang Commandery and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 後死於晉陽。

translations.literal: Later he died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 尒朱彥伯，榮從弟也。

translations.literal: Erzhu Yanbo was Rong's younger cousin by the collateral line.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Yanbo was a younger cousin of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 祖侯真，高祖時并安二州刺史、始昌侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hou Zhen, in the time of Emperor Gaozu, was Governor of both Bing and An provinces and Marquis of Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hou Zhen had served under Emperor Gaozu as Governor of Bing and An provinces and as Marquis of Shichang.

sentences.zh: 父買珍，世宗時武衞將軍，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Maizhen, in the time of Emperor Shizong, was General of the Martial Guard and went out to serve as Governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maizhen had been General of the Martial Guard under Emperor Shizong and was later sent out to govern Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 彥伯性和厚，釋褐奉朝請，累遷奉車都尉，為榮府長史。

translations.literal: Yanbo's nature was generous and mild. He entered service as a Gentleman Attendant at Court, was promoted through successive ranks to Commandant of the Imperial Chariots, and became Chief Clerk of Rong's princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Yanbo was warm and steady by nature. He began his career as a court attendant, rose to Commandant of the Imperial Chariots, and served as chief clerk in Erzhu Rong's household.

sentences.zh: 元曄立，以為侍中。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Yanbo was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye took the throne, Yanbo was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝潛默龍花佛寺，彥伯敦喻往來，尤有勤款。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor feigned mutism at Longhua Buddhist Temple; Yanbo earnestly admonished and counseled him in their coming and going, showing especial sincerity and devotion.
translations.idiomatic: While the Former Deposed Emperor kept up his pretense of silence at Longhua Temple, Yanbo visited him repeatedly with earnest persuasion and showed him unusual loyalty.

sentences.zh: 廢帝既立，尒朱兆以己不預謀，大為忿恚，將攻世隆。

translations.literal: Once the deposed emperor had been enthroned, Erzhu Zhao, because he had not taken part in the plot, was greatly enraged and was about to attack Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: After the Former Deposed Emperor was enthroned, Zhao flew into a rage at having been left out of the conspiracy and prepared to attack Shilong.

sentences.zh: 詔令華山王鷙兼尚書僕射、北道大使慰喻兆，兆猶不釋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Huashan Zhi to serve concurrently as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Northern Route Grand Commissioner to soothe and persuade Zhao, but Zhao still would not relent.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Prince of Huashan Zhi, concurrently Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Northern Route envoy, to reason with Zhao, but Zhao still refused to stand down.

sentences.zh: 世隆復遣彥伯自往喻之，兆乃止。

translations.literal: Shilong again sent Yanbo to go in person to explain matters to him, and Zhao then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong sent Yanbo to Zhao in person, and only then did Zhao halt his advance.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝醼彥伯於顯陽殿。

translations.literal: When he returned, the emperor banqueted Yanbo at the Xianyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On Yanbo's return, the emperor held a feast for him in the Xianyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 時侍中源子恭、黃門郎竇瑗並侍坐，彥伯曰：「源侍中比為都督，與臣相持於河內，當爾之時，旗鼓相望，眇如天隔，寧期同事陛下今日之歡也。」

translations.literal: At the time Palace Attendant Yuan Zigon and Yellow Gate Gentleman Dou Yuan were both seated in attendance. Yanbo said: "Palace Attendant Yuan, when you lately served as area commander, you and I faced each other at stalemate in Henei. In those days our banners and drums faced one another, distant as heaven itself. Who could have expected that we would now share in Your Majesty's joy of today?"
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yuan Zigon and Yellow Gate Gentleman Dou Yuan were also present. Yanbo said, "Palace Attendant Yuan, when you were area commander we faced each other across the lines at Henei. Our camps were worlds apart then. Who would have guessed we would drink together at the emperor's table today?"

sentences.zh: 子恭曰：「蒯通有言，犬吠非其主。

translations.literal: Zigon said: "Kuai Tong had a saying: a dog barks not for its proper master.
translations.idiomatic: Zigon replied, "Kuai Tong once said that a dog barks for whoever is its master.

sentences.zh: 他日之事永安，猶今日之事陛下耳。」

translations.literal: Serving Yong'an in days past is just like serving Your Majesty today."
translations.idiomatic: Serving Prince of Yong'an then is no different from serving Your Majesty now."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「源侍中可謂有射鈎之心也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Palace Attendant Yuan may truly be said to have the heart of Shegou."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Palace Attendant Yuan truly has the loyalty of one who once drew a hook-tipped arrow against his lord."

sentences.zh: 遂令二人極醉而罷。

translations.literal: He then had the two men drink to the point of complete intoxication and dismissed the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: He then had the two men drink until they were thoroughly drunk and ended the banquet.

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節、驃騎大將軍、右光祿大夫、馬場大都督，封博陵郡開國公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grandee of Splendid Virtue of the Right, Grand Commander of the Horse Pastures, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Boling Commandery with a state-founding fief.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Yanbo received the staff of authority as Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grandee of Splendid Virtue of the Right, and Grand Commander of the Horse Pastures, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 後進爵為王。

translations.literal: Later his noble rank was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was later raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 又遷司徒，于時炎旱，有勸彥伯解司徒者，乃上表遜位，詔許之。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the post of Minister over the Masses. At that time there was scorching drought, and some urged Yanbo to relinquish the Ministry; he thereupon submitted a memorial yielding the office, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made Minister over the Masses. During a severe drought some advised Yanbo to step down from the ministry; he submitted a resignation, and the emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 俄除儀同三司、侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Grandee Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 彥伯於兄弟之中，差無過患。

translations.literal: Among the brothers, Yanbo had comparatively few excesses or faults.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Erzhu brothers, Yanbo was relatively free of serious wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 天光等敗於韓陵，彥伯欲領兵屯河橋以為聲勢，世隆不從。

translations.literal: When Tianguang and the others were defeated at Hanling, Yanbo wished to lead troops to encamp at Heqiao to create a show of force, but Shilong would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianguang's defeat at Hanling, Yanbo wanted to take troops to Heqiao and make a stand, but Shilong refused.

sentences.zh: 及張勸等掩襲世隆，[3]彥伯時在禁直從。

translations.literal: When Zhang Quan and the others made a surprise attack on Shilong, [3] Yanbo was at the time on palace duty in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Quan and his men seized Shilong by surprise, [3] Yanbo happened to be on duty in the palace.

sentences.zh: 長孫稚等於神虎門啟陳齊獻武王義功既振，將除尒朱。

translations.literal: Changsun Zhi and the others reported at the Divine Tiger Gate that the Prince of Qi, Xianwu, had already raised righteous merit and was about to eliminate the Erzhu.
translations.idiomatic: At the Divine Tiger Gate, Changsun Zhi reported that Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu, had already triumphed and was preparing to destroy the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 廢帝令舍人郭崇報彥伯知。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Attendant Guo Chong to inform Yanbo of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Guo Chong to warn Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 彥伯狼狽出走，為人所執。

translations.literal: Yanbo fled in panic and was seized by others.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo bolted in disarray and was captured.

sentences.zh: 尋與世隆同斬於閶闔門外，懸首於斛斯椿門樹，傳首於齊獻武王。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was beheaded together with Shilong outside the Changhe Gate; his head was hung on the gate tree at Husi Chun's residence and sent on to the Prince of Qi, Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon beheaded with Shilong outside the Changhe Gate. His head was hung on the tree by Husi Chun's gate and then sent to Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 先是，洛中謠曰：「三月末，四月初，揚灰簸土覔真珠。」

translations.literal: Earlier, a rhyme in Luoyang said: "At the end of the third month and the beginning of the fourth month, raise dust and sift earth looking for pearls."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a song in Luoyang had run: "Late in the third month, early in the fourth, raise dust and sift the soil hunting pearls."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「頭去項，脚根齊，驅上樹，不須梯。」

translations.literal: It also said: "The head leaves the neck, the feet level with the roots; drive him up a tree—no ladder needed."
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "Head parted from neck, feet flush with the roots; hoist him up a tree without a ladder."

sentences.zh: 至是並驗。

translations.literal: When the time came, both were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came, both prophecies proved true.

sentences.zh: 彥伯弟仲遠，頗知書計。

translations.literal: Yanbo's younger brother Zhongyuan was fairly skilled in writing and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo's younger brother Zhongyuan was literate and good with accounts.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末年，尒朱榮兵威稍盛，諸有啟謁，率多見從。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Suzong, Erzhu Rong's military power gradually grew stronger, and most petitions and requests submitted to him were generally granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Emperor Suzong's reign, Rong's military power grew, and most petitions brought to him were approved.

sentences.zh: 而仲遠摹寫榮書，又刻榮印，與尚書令史通為姦詐，造榮啟表，請人為官，大得財貨，以資酒色，落魄無行。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan, however, copied Rong's letters and also carved Rong's seal; he conspired in fraud with clerks of the Masters of Writing, forged memorials from Rong requesting appointments for people, and obtained great wealth, which he spent on wine and women. He was dissolute and without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan copied Rong's correspondence, carved a counterfeit of his seal, and conspired with Masters of Writing clerks to forge Rong's memorials recommending men for office. He amassed a fortune, squandered it on wine and women, and lived as a reckless wastrel.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊即阼，除直寢、寧遠將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Zhongyuan was appointed Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuang Emperor took the throne, Zhongyuan was made Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 尋特除平北將軍、建興太守，頓丘縣開國侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was specially appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Jianxing, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dunqiu County with a state-founding fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon specially appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Jianxing, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dunqiu with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及改郡立州，遷使持節、車騎將軍、建州刺史。

translations.literal: When commanderies were changed into provinces, he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of Jian Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the administrative districts were reorganized from commanderies into provinces, he became Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of Jian Province.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，進爵為公，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was given the additional post of Palace Attendant, his noble rank was advanced to duke, and his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Palace Attendant, raised to ducal rank, and given five hundred additional fief households.

sentences.zh: 尋改封清河郡，又加車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his fief was changed to Qinghe Commandery, and he was additionally appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grandee of Splendid Virtue of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was soon changed to Qinghe Commandery, and he received the additional ranks of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grandee of Splendid Virtue of the Left.

sentences.zh: 轉使持節、本將軍、徐州刺史、兼尚書左僕射、三徐州大行臺。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, his original generalship, Governor of Xu Province, concurrently Vice Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner of the Great Office for the Three Xu Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Governor of Xu Province, while retaining his general's rank and serving concurrently as Vice Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing and head of the Eastern Route Grand Office for the three Xu provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋進督三徐州諸軍事，餘如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to command all military affairs of the Three Xu Provinces; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of all military affairs in the three Xu provinces; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 仲遠上言曰：「將統參佐，人數不足，事須在道更僕以充其員。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan submitted a memorial saying: "The generals' staffs and aides are insufficient in number; it is necessary to replace and appoint men along the route to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan memorialized the throne: "My staff officers are too few. I need authority to appoint replacements along the march to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 竊見比來行臺採募者皆得權立中正，在軍定第，斟酌授官。

translations.literal: I have privately observed that recently those recruited by the Eastern Route Office have all been allowed to establish zhongzheng officers on a provisional basis, fix grades in the army, and confer offices after deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I note that recent recruits under the Eastern Route Office have been allowed to set up provisional zhongzheng officers, rank men in camp, and assign posts as they see fit.

sentences.zh: 今求兼置，權濟軍要。」

translations.literal: I now request to be additionally granted the same arrangement, as a provisional measure to meet military needs."
translations.idiomatic: I ask for the same authority now, as a temporary measure to meet the army's needs."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 於是隨情補授，肆意聚斂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed men as he pleased and extorted wealth without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He then handed out offices at whim and plundered without restraint.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮死，仲遠勒眾來向京師，攻陷西兗州，將逼東郡。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Zhongyuan drove his forces toward the capital, captured Western Yan Province, and was about to press on into Eastern Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death, Zhongyuan marched on the capital with his army, seized Western Yan Province, and threatened Eastern Commandery.

sentences.zh: 莊帝詔諸督將駱驛進討，並為仲遠所敗。

translations.literal: The Zhuang Emperor ordered the various area commanders and generals to advance in rapid succession to attack him, but all were defeated by Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuang Emperor ordered his commanders to pursue Zhongyuan in forced marches, but Zhongyuan defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 又詔都督鄭先護及右衞將軍賀拔勝共討之。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered Area Commander Zheng Xianhu and General of the Right Guard Helaba Sheng to join in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Area Commander Zheng Xianhu and General of the Right Guard Helaba Sheng to attack him together.

sentences.zh: 勝戰不利，仍降仲遠。

translations.literal: Sheng fought without success and thereupon surrendered to Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was beaten in battle and went over to Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 尋尒朱兆入洛，先護眾散而走。

translations.literal: Before long Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Xianhu's forces scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhao entered Luoyang, and Xianhu's army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝立，除使持節，侍中，都督三徐、二兗諸軍事，驃騎大將軍，開府儀同三司，徐州刺史，東道大都督，大行臺，進爵彭城王。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor was enthroned, Zhongyuan was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander of All Military Affairs of the Three Xu and Two Yan Provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grandee with an Office Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, Governor of Xu Province, Grand Commander of the Eastern Route, Grand Commissioner of the Great Office, and his noble rank was advanced to Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Zhongyuan received the staff of authority as Palace Attendant, commander of the three Xu and two Yan provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, governor of Xu Province, head of the Eastern Route and of the Grand Office, and was raised to Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 尋加大將軍，又兼尚書令。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given the additional rank of Grand General and was concurrently appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand General and concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 竟不之州，遂鎮於大梁。

translations.literal: In the end he never went to the province and instead established his headquarters at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: He never went to his province at all and instead made his base at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 仲遠遣使請準朝式，在軍鳴騶。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan sent envoys requesting permission to follow court protocol and to have outriders announce his approach while in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan asked permission to follow full court protocol and to have heralds clear the road for him even in camp.

sentences.zh: 帝覽啟，笑而許之。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial, laughed, and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the request, laughed, and approved it.

sentences.zh: 其肆情如此。

translations.literal: His willfulness was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: That was how far his arrogance went.

sentences.zh: 復進督東道諸軍、本將軍、兗州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to command all armies of the Eastern Route, retain his original generalship, and serve as Governor of Yan Province; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made commander of all Eastern Route armies and Governor of Yan Province while keeping his other titles.

sentences.zh: 仲遠天性貪暴，大宗富族，誣之以反，歿其家口，簿籍財物，皆以入己，丈夫死者投之河流，如此者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan was greedy and violent by nature. Great clans and wealthy families he falsely accused of rebellion, wiped out their households, registered their goods and wealth, and took everything for himself. Men who were killed he cast into the river; cases such as these were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan was greedy and brutal by nature. He framed great clans and rich families for treason, exterminated their households, seized their property, and kept it all for himself. The men he killed he threw into the river; there were more victims than anyone could count.

sentences.zh: 諸將婦有美色者，莫不被其淫亂。

translations.literal: Among the generals' wives who had beautiful looks, none escaped his debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: No attractive general's wife escaped his abuse.

sentences.zh: 自滎陽以東，輸稅悉入其軍，不送京師。

translations.literal: From Xingyang eastward, all delivered taxes went entirely into his army and were not sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From Xingyang eastward, all tax revenues went to his army instead of the capital.

sentences.zh: 時天光控關右，仲遠在大梁，兆據并州，世隆居京邑，各自專恣，權強莫比焉。

translations.literal: At that time Tianguang controlled the lands west of the passes, Zhongyuan was at Daliang, Zhao held Bing Province, and Shilong resided in the capital region; each acted with unchecked willfulness, and their power had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang held the northwest, Zhongyuan ruled from Daliang, Zhao controlled Bing Province, and Shilong dominated the capital. Each ruled like a petty tyrant, and none could match their combined power.

sentences.zh: 所在並以貪虐為事，於是四方解體。

translations.literal: Everywhere they made greed and cruelty their business, and so the realm fell apart on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere they ruled through greed and cruelty, and the empire began to come apart.

sentences.zh: 又加太宰，解大行臺。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Grand Preceptor and relieved of the Grand Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Grand Preceptor and relieved of the Grand Office.

sentences.zh: 仲遠專恣尤劇，方之彥伯、世隆最為無禮，東南牧守下至民俗，比之豺狼，特為患苦。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's willfulness was especially extreme; compared with Yanbo and Shilong he was the most insolent. From the governors and administrators of the southeast down to the common people, people likened him to wolves and jackals, and he caused suffering above all others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan was the worst of the lot—even more overbearing than Yanbo or Shilong. From southeastern officials down to ordinary people, he was compared to wolves and jackals, and he brought suffering above all the rest.

sentences.zh: 後移屯東郡，率眾與度律等拒齊獻武王。

translations.literal: Later he moved his camp to Eastern Commandery and led his forces with Dulu and the others to resist the Prince of Qi, Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: He later shifted his camp to Eastern Commandery and joined Dulu and the others in opposing Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆領騎數千自晉陽來會，軍次陽平，王縱以間說，仲遠等迭相猜疑，狼狽遁走。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao led several thousand horsemen from Jinyang to join him. When the army halted at Yangping, the prince spread disinformation; Zhongyuan and the others grew mutually suspicious in turn and fled in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao came from Jinyang with several thousand horsemen to join him. At Yangping, Gao Huan spread rumors to sow discord; Zhongyuan and his allies turned on one another in suspicion and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 後與天光等於韓陵戰敗，南走東郡，仍奔蕭衍。

translations.literal: Later he was defeated together with Tianguang and the others at Hanling, fled south to Eastern Commandery, and then went over to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After he and Tianguang were defeated at Hanling, he fled south to Eastern Commandery and then defected to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 死於江南。

translations.literal: He died in the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the south.

sentences.zh: 仲遠弟世隆，字榮宗。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's younger brother Shilong had the style name Rongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan's younger brother Shilong, styled Rongzong.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，為直齋。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Suzong's reign he served as Direct Attendant of the Fast.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Suzong's reign he served as Direct Attendant of the Fast.

sentences.zh: 轉直寢，後兼直閤，加前將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters, later served concurrently as Direct Attendant of the Pavilion, and was given the additional rank of General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He became Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters, later also Direct Attendant of the Pavilion, and was given the rank of General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮表請入朝，靈太后惡之，令世隆詣晉陽慰喻榮，榮因欲留之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong submitted a memorial requesting entry into court. Empress Dowager Ling hated this and ordered Shilong to go to Jinyang to soothe and persuade Rong, but Rong then wished to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong petitioned to enter the capital, Empress Dowager Ling distrusted him and sent Shilong to Jinyang to reason with him. Rong then tried to keep Shilong there.

sentences.zh: 世隆曰：「朝廷疑兄，故令世隆來，今若遂住，便有內備，非計之善者。」

translations.literal: Shilong said: "The court suspects my elder brother, and that is why it sent me. If I now stay on, the court will take internal precautions, and that is not a good plan."
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said, "The court distrusts you—that is why I was sent. If I stay, the court will go on alert at home, and that is a poor plan."

sentences.zh: 榮乃遣之。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Rong let him go.

sentences.zh: 榮舉兵南出，世隆遂遁走，會榮於上黨。

translations.literal: When Rong raised troops and marched south, Shilong fled and joined Rong at Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong marched south with his army, Shilong slipped away and rejoined him at Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，乃特除侍中、領軍將軍、左衞將軍、領左右、肆州大中正，封樂平郡開國公，食邑一千二百戶。

translations.literal: When the Zhuang Emperor ascended the throne, Shilong was specially appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Leads the Army, General of the Left Guard, Commander of the Left and Right, Chief Rectifier of Si Province, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Leping Commandery with a state-founding fief of one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuang Emperor took the throne, Shilong was specially made Palace Attendant, General Who Leads the Army, General of the Left Guard, and commander of the left and right guards, with the title of Chief Rectifier of Si Province, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Leping with a fief of twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又除車騎將軍、兼領軍，俄授左光祿大夫、兼尚書右僕射，尋即真。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and concurrently General Who Leads the Army; soon afterward he was given the posts of Grandee of Splendid Virtue of the Left and concurrently Vice Director of the Right of the Masters of Writing, and before long received the substantive appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made General of Chariots and Cavalry while retaining command of the army, then Grandee of Splendid Virtue of the Left and concurrently Vice Director of the Right of the Masters of Writing, and soon received those posts in full.

sentences.zh: 元顥逼大梁，詔假儀同三司、前軍都督，鎮虎牢。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed on Daliang, an edict provisionally granted Shilong the honor of Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers and the post of Area Commander of the Vanguard, and ordered him to garrison Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao threatened Daliang, Shilong was provisionally made Grandee Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers and Vanguard area commander and ordered to hold Hulao.

sentences.zh: 世隆不關世事，無將帥之略。

translations.literal: Shilong paid no attention to affairs of the age and had no strategy of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong took no interest in public affairs and had no talent for command.

sentences.zh: 顥既克滎陽，擒行臺楊昱，[4]世隆懼而遁還。

translations.literal: Once Hao had captured Xingyang and seized Eastern Route Commissioner Yang Yu, [4] Shilong was afraid and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao took Xingyang and captured Eastern Route Commissioner Yang Yu, [4] Shilong panicked and abandoned his post.

sentences.zh: 莊帝倉卒北巡，世隆之罪也。

translations.literal: The Zhuang Emperor's hasty northern tour was Shilong's fault.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuang Emperor's sudden flight north was Shilong's doing.

sentences.zh: 駕在河內，假驃騎大將軍、行臺右僕射、都督相州諸軍事、相州刺史、當州都督。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Henei, Shilong was provisionally appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Vice Director of the Right of the Eastern Route Office, Commander of All Military Affairs of Xiang Province, Governor of Xiang Province, and Area Commander of that province.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Henei, Shilong was provisionally made Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Vice Director of the Right of the Eastern Route Office, commander of Xiang Province's armies, and Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還宮，除驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射，攝選，左右廂出入。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, he was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Vice Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing, acted in charge of selection, and controlled entry and exit through the left and right side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, Shilong was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Vice Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing, placed in charge of official selection, and given control over access through the palace side chambers.

sentences.zh: 又以停年格取士，頗為猥滯所稱。

translations.literal: He also selected officials by the seniority-based appointment standard, and this was fairly praised by the vulgar and the mediocre.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed men by seniority under the tingnian system, which earned him praise from the mediocre and the cautious.

sentences.zh: 又請解侍中，詔加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He again requested to be relieved of the post of Palace Attendant, and an edict additionally appointed him Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to be relieved of the Palace Attendant post and was given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊帝之將圖尒朱榮也，或有牓世隆門以陳其狀者，世隆封以呈榮，勸其不入。

translations.literal: When the Zhuang Emperor was about to plot against Erzhu Rong, someone posted a notice on Shilong's gate stating the plan. Shilong sealed it and presented it to Rong, urging him not to enter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuang Emperor was plotting against Rong, someone posted a notice on Shilong's gate describing the plan. Shilong sealed it, showed it to Rong, and urged him not to enter the capital.

sentences.zh: 榮自恃威強，不以為意，遂手毀密書，唾地曰：「世隆無膽，誰敢生心！」

translations.literal: Rong, relying on his own overwhelming power, paid it no heed. He tore up the secret letter with his own hand, spat on the ground, and said: "Shilong has no courage—who would dare harbor such a thought!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong, confident in his power, ignored the warning. He tore up the letter, spat on the ground, and said, "Shilong hasn't the nerve for treason—who would dare move against me?"

sentences.zh: 及榮死，世隆奉榮妻，燒西陽門率眾夜走，北攻河橋，殺武衞將軍奚毅，率眾還戰大夏門外。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Shilong escorted Rong's wife, burned the Xiyang Gate, led his forces in flight by night, attacked Heqiao from the north, killed General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, and then led his troops back to fight outside the Daxia Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong was killed, Shilong escorted Rong's wife, burned the Xiyang Gate, fled by night with his troops, attacked Heqiao from the north, killed General of the Martial Guard Xi Yi, and then turned back to fight outside the Daxia Gate.

sentences.zh: 朝野震懼，憂在不測。

translations.literal: Court and countryside were shaken with fear, and people worried that disaster could not be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country were terrified, fearing the worst.

sentences.zh: 莊帝遣前華陽太守段育慰喻，世隆斬之以徇。

translations.literal: The Zhuang Emperor sent former Administrator of Huayang Duan Yu to soothe and persuade him, but Shilong beheaded Yu and displayed the head as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuang Emperor sent former Administrator of Huayang Duan Yu to negotiate with him, but Shilong executed Yu and displayed his head.

sentences.zh: 會李苗燒絕河梁，世隆乃北遁。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Miao burned and cut off the river bridge, and Shilong thereupon fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao burned the river bridge, and Shilong fled north.

sentences.zh: 建州刺史陸希質閉城拒守，世隆攻克之，盡殺城人以肆其忿。

translations.literal: Governor of Jian Province Lu Xizhi closed the city and resisted. Shilong captured it and killed everyone in the city to vent his rage.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Jian Province Lu Xizhi shut the city and resisted, but Shilong took it and slaughtered the entire population in revenge.

sentences.zh: 及至長子，與度律等共推長廣王曄為主，曄以世隆為開府儀同三司、尚書令、樂平郡王，加太傅，行司州牧，增邑五千戶。

translations.literal: When he reached Changzi, he joined with Dulu and the others in elevating Prince of Changguang Ye as leader. Ye appointed Shilong Grandee with an Office Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Leping Commandery, gave him the additional rank of Grand Tutor and Acting Governor of Si Province, and increased his fief by five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At Changzi he joined Dulu and the others in proclaiming Prince of Changguang Ye as ruler. Ye made Shilong Grandee Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Leping, with the additional titles of Grand Tutor and Acting Governor of Si Province, and added five thousand households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 先赴京師，會兆於河陽。

translations.literal: He went first to the capital and met Zhao at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went on ahead to the capital and met Zhao at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 兆既平京邑，自以為功，讓世隆曰：「叔父在朝多時，耳目應廣，如何不知不聞，令天柱受禍！」

translations.literal: Once Zhao had pacified the capital region, he considered the achievement his own and reproached Shilong, saying: "Uncle, you were at court for many days; your eyes and ears should have been wide. How could you neither know nor hear, and let the State Pillar suffer disaster!"
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao pacified the capital, he took credit for the victory and rebuked Shilong: "You were at court for years, Uncle—your eyes and ears should have been everywhere. How could you have known nothing and let the State Pillar die?"

sentences.zh: 按劍瞋目，聲色甚厲。

translations.literal: He grasped his sword, glared with angry eyes, and his voice and expression were very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He gripped his sword, glared, and spoke in a voice of fury.

sentences.zh: 世隆遜辭拜謝，然後得已。

translations.literal: Shilong yielded with humble words and bowed in apology, and only then was Zhao satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong apologized humbly, and only then did Zhao let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 世隆深恨之。

translations.literal: Shilong deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong nursed a deep grudge over the incident.

sentences.zh: 時仲遠亦自滑臺入京，世隆與兄弟密謀，以元曄疏遠，欲推立前廢帝。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongyuan also entered the capital from Huatai. Shilong secretly plotted with his brothers that, because Yuan Ye was distant and estranged, they wished to elevate the Former Deposed Emperor instead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan had also entered the capital from Huatai. Shilong and his brothers secretly agreed that Yuan Ye was too remote a figure and planned to put the Former Deposed Emperor on the throne instead.

sentences.zh: 而尒朱度律意在寶炬，乃曰：「廣陵不言，何以主天下？」

translations.literal: But Erzhu Dulu's intention favored Baoju, and he said: "If Guangling does not speak, how can he rule the world?"
translations.idiomatic: But Dulu favored Baoju and objected: "If Guangling will not speak, how can he rule the realm?"

sentences.zh: 世隆兄彥伯密相敦喻，乃與度律同往龍花佛寺觀之，後知能語，遂行廢立。

translations.literal: Shilong's elder brother Yanbo secretly exhorted and persuaded one another, then together with Dulu went to Longhua Buddhist Temple to observe him. Later, learning that he could speak, they thereupon carried out the deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's brother Yanbo persuaded him in private, then went with Dulu to Longhua Buddhist Temple to see the Former Deposed Emperor. Once they confirmed that he could speak, they proceeded with the deposition and restoration.

sentences.zh: 初，世隆之為僕射，自憂不了，乃取尚書文簿在家省閱。

translations.literal: At first, when Shilong became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, he worried that he could not manage the office and took the Ministry archives home to review them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilong first became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, he feared he was not up to the post and brought the Ministry's case files home to study.

sentences.zh: 性聰解，積十餘日，然後視事。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick-witted; he accumulated more than ten days of study, and only then took up his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted by nature, he spent more than ten days at home before he finally took office.

sentences.zh: 又畏尒朱榮威，深自克勉，留心几案，傍接賓客，遂有解了之名。

translations.literal: He also feared Erzhu Rong's authority, deeply restrained himself, kept his mind on the desk, received guests on all sides, and thereby gained a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He also feared Rong's power, so he applied himself rigorously, kept close watch over his paperwork, and received guests attentively until he earned a name for being capable.

sentences.zh: 榮死之後，無所顧憚。

translations.literal: After Rong died, there was nothing left for him to fear.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death, he no longer had anything to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 及為尚書令，常使尚書郎宋遊道、邢昕在其宅廳視事，東西別坐，受納訴訟，稱命施行。

translations.literal: When he became Director of the Masters of Writing, he regularly had Secretariat Attendants Song Youdao and Xing Xin conduct affairs in the hall of his residence, sitting separately east and west, receiving and accepting lawsuits, and issuing orders in his name.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became Director of the Masters of Writing, he routinely had Secretariat Attendants Song Youdao and Xing Xin hold court in the hall of his own residence, seated apart east and west, taking petitions and issuing orders as though from his own hand.

sentences.zh: 其專恣如此。

translations.literal: His arbitrary self-will was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the extent of his arbitrary rule.

sentences.zh: 既總朝政，生殺自由，公行淫佚，無復畏避，信任羣小，隨其與奪。

translations.literal: Once he controlled court politics, life and death were at his free disposal; he openly indulged in debauchery without further restraint or fear, trusted petty men, and granted or seized at will.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the reins of government, he disposed of lives as he pleased, indulged his appetites openly, and no longer held back. He put his trust in petty men and gave or took away whatever he wished.

sentences.zh: 又欲收軍人之意，加汎除授，皆以將軍而兼散職，督將兵吏無虛號者。

translations.literal: He also wished to win over the soldiers' hearts, so he broadly granted appointments: all were made generals with concurrent honorary posts, and among officers, commanders, soldiers, and clerks none lacked a title.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to win the army's loyalty, he handed out appointments indiscriminately. Every man received a general's rank with some additional honorary post, so that among officers, commanders, soldiers, and clerks there was scarcely a man without a title.

sentences.zh: 自此五等大夫，遂致猥濫，又無員限，天下賤之。

translations.literal: From this the fifth-rank grandees became vulgarly abundant, and there was no quota limit; all under Heaven despised it.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the fifth-rank grandee titles became debased and overused, with no limit on numbers, and the empire held the practice in contempt.

sentences.zh: 武定中，齊文襄奏皆罷，於是始革其弊。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, the Prince Wenxiang of Qi memorialized that all should be abolished, and only then was the abuse first reformed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding reign, Gao Cheng, Prince Wenxiang of Qi, memorialized to abolish the practice entirely, and only then was the abuse finally corrected.

sentences.zh: 世隆兄弟羣從，各擁強兵，割剝四海，極其暴虐。

translations.literal: Shilong's brothers and clan cousins each held strong armies, stripped and exploited all within the Four Seas, and carried their brutality to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's brothers and kinsmen each commanded powerful armies, plundered the empire, and carried their cruelty to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 姦諂蛆酷多見信用，[5]溫良名士罕預腹心。

translations.literal: Treacherous flatterers and cruel sycophants were widely trusted, [5] while gentle upright men of note were rarely admitted to his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers, schemers, and cruel toadies won his trust, [5] while upright scholars of gentle character were seldom admitted to his confidence.

sentences.zh: 於是天下之人莫不厭毒。

translations.literal: Thereupon none under Heaven failed to loathe them with disgust.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven came to loathe them.

sentences.zh: 世隆尋讓太傅，改授太保，又固辭，前廢帝特置儀同三師之官，次上公之下，以世隆為之。

translations.literal: Shilong soon yielded the Grand Tutorship and was reassigned as Grand Preceptor, but again firmly declined. The Former Deposed Emperor specially created the office of Three Masters Equal in Honor, ranking below the highest dukes, and made Shilong hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong soon resigned as Grand Tutor and was offered Grand Preceptor instead, but declined that as well. The Former Deposed Emperor then created a special post of Three Masters Equal in Honor, ranking just below the highest dukes, and appointed Shilong to it.

sentences.zh: 贈其父買珍使持節、侍中、相國、錄尚書事、都督定相青齊濟五州諸軍事、大司馬、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father Maizhen as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for the five provinces of Ding, Xiang, Qing, Qi, and Ji, Grand Marshal, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his father Maizhen with the titles of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Ding, Xiang, Qing, Qi, and Ji provinces, Grand Marshal, and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 及齊獻武王起義兵，仲遠、度律等愚戇，恃強不以為慮，而世隆獨深憂恐。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi, Xianwu, raised a righteous army, Zhongyuan, Dulu, and the others were stupid and reckless, relying on their strength and giving it no thought, while Shilong alone was deeply worried and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu, raised the banner of revolt, Zhongyuan and Dulu were dull and overconfident, trusting in their strength and giving the threat little thought, while Shilong alone was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 及天光戰敗，世隆請出收兵，前廢帝不許。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was defeated in battle, Shilong requested permission to go out and gather troops, but the Former Deposed Emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianguang's defeat, Shilong asked to go out and rally the troops, but the Former Deposed Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 世隆令其外兵參軍陽叔淵單騎馳赴北中，簡閱敗眾，以次內之。

translations.literal: Shilong ordered his External Affairs Military Aide Yang Shuyuan to ride alone at full speed to the North Gate, review the defeated troops, and admit them in order.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong sent his external affairs aide Yang Shuyuan riding alone to the North Gate to review the defeated troops and admit them one by one.

sentences.zh: 而斛斯椿未得入城，詭說叔淵曰：「天光部下皆是西人，聞其欲掠京邑，遷都長安。

translations.literal: But Helaba Chun had not yet been admitted into the city and deceptively told Shuyuan: "Tianguang's subordinates are all westerners. I have heard that they intend to plunder the capital and move the court to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Helaba Chun had not yet entered the city. He lied to Shuyuan, saying, "Tianguang's men are all westerners. I hear they mean to plunder the capital and move the court to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 宜先內我，以為其備。」

translations.literal: You should first admit me, to serve as a guard against them."
translations.idiomatic: Admit me first, so I can stand guard against them."

sentences.zh: 叔淵信而內之。

translations.literal: Shuyuan believed him and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyuan believed him and let him in.

sentences.zh: 椿既至橋，盡殺世隆黨附，令行臺長孫稚詣闕奏狀，別使都督賈智、張勸率騎掩執世隆與兄彥伯，俱斬之。

translations.literal: Once Chun reached the bridge, he killed all of Shilong's partisans, ordered Branch Secretariat Chief Changsun Zhi to go to the palace and report the facts, and separately sent Commanders Jia Zhi and Zhang Quan with cavalry to seize Shilong and his elder brother Yanbo by surprise; both were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chun reached the bridge, he slaughtered Shilong's followers, sent Branch Secretariat Chief Changsun Zhi to the palace to report what had happened, and dispatched Commanders Jia Zhi and Zhang Quan with cavalry to seize Shilong and his brother Yanbo. Both were executed.

sentences.zh: 時年三十三。

translations.literal: He was thirty-three years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 初，世隆曾與吏部尚書元世儁握槊，忽聞局上歘然有聲，一局之子盡皆倒立，世隆甚惡之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shilong had once played the board game with Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun when suddenly a whooshing sound was heard on the board and every piece on the board stood upside down. Shilong greatly hated the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shilong had been playing a board game with Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun when every piece on the board suddenly flipped over with a sharp crack. Shilong took it as a terrible omen.

sentences.zh: 世隆又曾晝寢，其妻奚氏忽見有一人持世隆首去，奚氏驚怖就視，而世隆寢如故也。

translations.literal: Shilong also once napped by day. His wife Lady Xi suddenly saw a man carrying Shilong's head away. Lady Xi was frightened and went to look, but Shilong was sleeping as before.
