translations.idiomatic: Shilong also once napped in the daytime. His wife Lady Xi suddenly saw a man carrying off Shilong's head. Terrified, she rushed to look, but Shilong was still asleep as before.

sentences.zh: 既覺，謂妻曰：「向夢人斷我頭去，意殊不適。」

translations.literal: When he awoke, he told his wife: "I just dreamed that someone cut off my head and carried it away. I feel very ill at ease."
translations.idiomatic: When he woke, he told his wife, "I dreamed just now that someone cut off my head and carried it away. I feel deeply unsettled."

sentences.zh: 又此年正月晦日，令、僕並不上省，西門不開。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the last day of the first month that year, neither the Director nor the Vice Director went to the office, and the west gate was not opened.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the first month that year, neither the Director nor the Vice Director reported to the office, and the west gate remained closed.

sentences.zh: 忽有河內太守田怗家奴告省門亭長云：[6]「今旦為令王借車牛一乘，終日於洛濱遊觀。

translations.literal: Suddenly a household slave of Governor of Henei Tian Tie reported to the provincial gate sentry chief, saying: [6] "This morning I lent one cart and ox to the Director-Prince. He spent the whole day touring along the Luo River bank.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a household slave of Governor of Henei Tian Tie came to the provincial gate sentry chief and said: [6] "This morning I lent a cart and ox to the Director-Prince, who spent the entire day sightseeing along the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 至晚，王還省，將車出東掖門，[7]始覺車上無褥，請為記識。」

translations.literal: By evening the Prince returned to the office and drove the cart out through the East Side Gate. [7] Only then did he notice there was no cushion on the cart and asked that this be recorded."
translations.idiomatic: In the evening the Prince returned to the office and drove the cart out through the East Side Gate. [7] Only then did he notice the cart had no cushion and asked that the matter be noted down."

sentences.zh: 時世隆封王，故呼為令王。

translations.literal: At that time Shilong had been enfeoffed as a prince, so he was called the Director-Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong had been enfeoffed as a prince, so he was called the Director-Prince.

sentences.zh: 亭長以令、僕不上，西門不開，無車入省，兼無車跡。

translations.literal: The sentry chief replied that neither the Director nor the Vice Director had reported to the office, the west gate had not been opened, no cart had entered the office, and moreover there were no cart tracks.
translations.idiomatic: The sentry chief replied that the Director and Vice Director had not reported to the office, the west gate had not been opened, no cart could have entered, and there were no cart tracks to be seen.

sentences.zh: 此奴固陳不已，公文列訴。

translations.literal: This slave persistently stated his account without stopping, and an official document was filed as a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The slave insisted on his story, and a formal complaint was entered on the record.

sentences.zh: 尚書都令史謝遠疑謂妄有假借，白世隆付曹推檢。

translations.literal: Secretariat Chief Clerk Xie Yuanyi suspected that the borrowing had been falsely claimed and reported to Shilong to hand the matter to the bureau for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Chief Clerk Xie Yuanyi suspected a false claim and reported the matter to Shilong, who ordered the appropriate bureau to investigate.

sentences.zh: 時都官郎穆子容窮究之，奴言：「初來時至司空府西，欲向省，令王嫌遲，遣二防閤捉儀刀催車。

translations.literal: At the time Capital Crimes Section Attendant Mu Zirong thoroughly investigated the matter. The slave said: "When I first arrived I reached the west of the Minister of Works' mansion and was heading toward the office. The Director-Prince, displeased at the delay, sent two guards with ceremonial swords to hurry the cart along.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Crimes Section Attendant Mu Zirong conducted a full inquiry. The slave said, "When I first arrived I reached the west side of the Minister of Works' mansion and was heading for the office. The Director-Prince, annoyed at the delay, sent two guards with ceremonial swords to hurry the cart along.

sentences.zh: 車入，到省西門，王嫌牛小，繫於闕下槐樹，更將一青牛駕車。

translations.literal: The cart entered and reached the west gate of the office. The Prince disliked the ox for being small, tied it beneath the locust tree under the gate tower, and switched to a blue ox to drive the cart.
translations.idiomatic: The cart entered and reached the west gate of the office. The Prince thought the ox too small, tied it beneath the locust tree at the gate tower, and switched to a blue ox to drive the cart.

sentences.zh: 令王著白紗高頂帽，短小黑色，[8]儐從皆裙襦袴褶，握板，不似常時服章。

translations.literal: The Director-Prince wore a white gauze high-peaked cap and short black clothing. [8] His attendants all wore skirted jackets and trousers, held tablets, and did not resemble their usual ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Director-Prince wore a white gauze high-peaked cap and short black garments. [8] His attendants all wore skirted jackets and trousers, carried tablets, and looked nothing like their usual ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 遂遣一吏將奴送入省中廳事東閤內東廂第一屋中。」

translations.literal: He then sent one clerk to escort the slave into the first room in the east wing inside the east pavilion of the central hall of the office."
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a clerk to escort the slave into the first room of the east wing inside the east pavilion of the office's central hall."

sentences.zh: 其屋先常閉籥。

translations.literal: That room had always been kept locked.
translations.idiomatic: That room had always been kept locked.

sentences.zh: 子容以西門不開，忽言從入；

translations.literal: Zirong, because the west gate had not been opened, seized on the claim that the slave had entered through it;
translations.idiomatic: Zirong, noting that the west gate had not been opened, challenged the claim that the slave had entered through it;

sentences.zh: 此屋常閉，奴言在中。

translations.literal: this room was always closed, yet the slave said he had been inside it.
translations.idiomatic: and because the room was always kept locked, he challenged the slave's claim that he had been inside.

sentences.zh: 詰其虛罔。

translations.literal: He interrogated him as to the falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed him on the impossibility of the story.

sentences.zh: 奴云：「此屋若閉，求得開看，屋中有一板牀，牀上無席，大有塵土，兼有一甕米。

translations.literal: The slave said: "If this room is closed, ask to open it and look. Inside there is a plank bed with no mat on it and much dust, and also one jar of rice.
translations.idiomatic: The slave said, "If the room is locked, open it and look. Inside you'll find a plank bed with no mat, thick with dust, and a jar of rice.

sentences.zh: 奴拂牀而坐，兼畫地戲弄，甕中之米亦握看之。

translations.literal: I brushed the bed and sat down, also drew on the ground in play, and grasped and looked at the rice in the jar as well.
translations.idiomatic: I brushed off the bed and sat down, scratched marks on the floor for amusement, and even picked up and examined the rice in the jar.

sentences.zh: 定其閉者，應無事驗。」

translations.literal: If it is determined to have been closed, there should be no evidence of these events."
translations.idiomatic: If the room has truly been shut all along, there should be no sign of any of this."

sentences.zh: 子容與謝遠自入看之，戶閉極久，全無開跡。

translations.literal: Zirong and Xie Yuan personally entered to look. The door had been closed for a very long time, and there was no trace of its having been opened.
translations.idiomatic: Zirong and Xie Yuan went in to look for themselves. The door had been shut for a long time, and there was no sign it had been opened.

sentences.zh: 及入，拂牀畫地，蹤緒歷然，米亦符同，方知不謬。

translations.literal: Once they entered, the traces of brushing the bed and drawing on the ground were clearly visible, and the rice also matched. Only then did they know the account was not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, they found the bed brushed clean and marks scratched on the floor exactly as described, and the rice matched as well. They knew then that the slave had not lied.

sentences.zh: 具以此對。

translations.literal: They fully reported this in reply.
translations.idiomatic: They reported all of this in full.

sentences.zh: 世隆悵然，意以為惡。

translations.literal: Shilong was frustrated and took it as an ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong was deeply unsettled and took it as a bad sign.

sentences.zh: 未幾見誅。

translations.literal: Before long he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 世隆弟世承。

translations.literal: Shilong's younger brother was Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong had a younger brother named Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，為寧朔將軍、步兵校尉，欒城縣開國伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhuang Emperor's reign, he served as General of Peaceful Campaigns, Colonel of Footsoldiers, and Baron of Luancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhuang Emperor's reign, he was made General of Peaceful Campaigns, Colonel of Footsoldiers, and Baron of Luancheng County.

sentences.zh: 又特除撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫、左衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was also specially appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Master of the Golden Crown and Purple Canopy, and General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also received special appointment as General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Master of the Golden Crown and Purple Canopy, and General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Palace Attendant and Inspector-General of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Attendant as well and appointed Inspector-General of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 世承人才猥劣，備員而已。

translations.literal: Shicheng's talent was base and inferior; he was a placeholder and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng was a man of mean ability and filled the post in name only.

sentences.zh: 及元顥內逼，詔世承守轘轅。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, an edict ordered Shicheng to defend Huanxuan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed inward toward the capital, an edict ordered Shicheng to hold Huanxuan Pass.

sentences.zh: 世隆棄虎牢，不暇追告，尋為元顥所擒，臠殺之。

translations.literal: Shilong abandoned Huber and had no time to notify him in pursuit. Before long Shicheng was captured by Yuan Hao and dismembered and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong abandoned Huber without time to warn him. Shicheng was soon captured by Yuan Hao and torn limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，贈使持節、都督冀州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司徒、冀州刺史，追封趙郡公。

translations.literal: When the Zhuang Emperor returned to the palace, he posthumously granted Shicheng the titles of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Ji Province, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Minister over the Masses, and Governor of Ji Province, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhuang Emperor returned to the palace, he posthumously honored Shicheng as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Ji Province, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Minister over the Masses, and Governor of Ji Province, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 世承弟弼，字輔伯。

translations.literal: Shicheng's younger brother was Bi, courtesy name Fubo.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng had a younger brother, Bi, whose courtesy name was Fubo.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，為散騎常侍、左衞將軍，封朝陽縣開國伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Former Deposed Emperor's reign, he served as Palace Attendant-Cavalier at Large, General of the Left Guard, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Chaoyang County.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Former Deposed Emperor's reign, he was made Palace Attendant-Cavalier at Large and General of the Left Guard, and enfeoffed as Baron of Chaoyang County.

sentences.zh: 又除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫、領左右，改封河間郡公。

translations.literal: He was also appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of the Left Splendor Canopy, Commander of the Left and Right, and his fief was changed to Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of the Left Splendor Canopy, and Commander of the Left and Right, and his title was raised to Duke of Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he became Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Grandee Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers with Bountiful Court, and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Grandee Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers with Bountiful Court, and Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 天光等之赴韓陵也，世隆以其府長史房謨兼尚書，為齊州行臺，召募士馬，以趣四瀆。

translations.literal: When Tianguang and the others went to Hanling, Shilong had his bureau chief Fang Mo serve concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing and as Qizhou Branch Secretariat, to raise troops and horses and hurry toward the Four Channels.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang and the others marched to Hanling, Shilong appointed his bureau chief Fang Mo concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing and head of the Qizhou Branch Secretariat to raise troops and hurry toward the Four Channels.

translations.literal: 〈Text missing.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Text missing.〉

sentences.zh: 弼總東陽之眾，亦赴亂城，

translations.literal: Bi gathered the forces of Dongyang and also hurried toward Luancheng,
translations.idiomatic: Bi gathered the forces of Dongyang and also marched toward Luancheng,

translations.literal: 〈Doubtful reading.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Doubtful reading.〉

sentences.zh: 揚聲北渡，以為掎角之勢。

translations.literal: Proclaiming a crossing north of the river, to create a pincer posture.
translations.idiomatic: Declaring that he would cross north of the river to form a pincer with the main force.

sentences.zh: 及天光等敗，弼乃還州。

translations.literal: When Tianguang and the others were defeated, Bi then returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianguang's defeat, Bi returned to his province.

sentences.zh: 世隆既擒，弼欲奔蕭衍，數與左右割臂為約。

translations.literal: After Shilong had been captured, Bi wished to flee to Xiao Yan and several times cut his arm with his companions to seal their covenant.
translations.idiomatic: After Shilong was captured, Bi planned to flee to Xiao Yan and repeatedly cut his arm with his close followers to bind them in oath.

sentences.zh: 弼帳下都督馮紹隆為弼信待，乃說弼曰：「今方同契闊，須更約盟。

translations.literal: Bi's headquarters commander Feng Shaolong, whom Bi trusted and favored, then urged Bi, saying: "Now that we share hardship together, we must renew our covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shaolong, a commander in Bi's camp whom Bi trusted, urged him, "We are bound together in hardship now. We must renew our oath.

sentences.zh: 宜可當心瀝血，示眾以信。」

translations.literal: You should pierce your heart and drip blood, to show the assembly your sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: You should pierce your heart and let the blood flow, to show the men your good faith."

sentences.zh: 弼乃從之，遂大集部下，弼乃踞胡牀，令紹隆持刀披心。

translations.literal: Bi thereupon complied. He then gathered all his subordinates in great assembly. Bi sat upon a camp chair and ordered Shaolong to take a knife and cut open his chest.
translations.idiomatic: Bi agreed. He assembled all his subordinates, sat on a camp chair, and ordered Shaolong to take a knife and cut open his chest.

sentences.zh: 紹隆因推刃殺之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Shaolong thereupon drove the blade forward and killed him, then sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolong drove the blade home and killed him, then sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尒朱度律，榮從父弟也。

translations.literal: Erzhu Dulu was Rong's father's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Dulu was a cousin of Rong's.

sentences.zh: 鄙朴少言。

translations.literal: He was crude and plain and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: He was coarse and plain-spoken and said little.

sentences.zh: 為統軍，從榮征伐。

translations.literal: As a commanding general, he followed Rong on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: As a commanding general, he followed Rong on campaign.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，除安西將軍、光祿大夫，封樂鄉縣開國伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhuang Emperor's reign, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Master of the Splendor Canopy, and enfeoffed as Baron of Lexiang County.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhuang Emperor's reign, he was made General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Master of the Splendor Canopy, and Baron of Lexiang County.

sentences.zh: 尋轉安北將軍、朔州刺史，復除軍州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Shuo Province, and was again appointed Governor of Jun Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Shuo Province, and later appointed Governor of Jun Province.

sentences.zh: [9]後加散騎常侍、右衞將軍。

translations.literal: [9] Later he was additionally made Palace Attendant-Cavalier at Large and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: [9] He was later made Palace Attendant-Cavalier at Large and General of the Right Guard as well.

sentences.zh: 又除衞將軍、左光祿大夫，兼京畿大都督。

translations.literal: He was also appointed General of the Guard, Grand Master of the Left Splendor Canopy, and concurrently Metropolitan Area Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made General of the Guard and Grand Master of the Left Splendor Canopy, and concurrently placed in command of the metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 榮死，與世隆赴晉陽。

translations.literal: After Rong died, he went with Shilong to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death, he went with Shilong to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 元曄之立，以度律為太尉公、四面大都督，封常山王。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was installed, Dulu was made Duke of Grand Commandant and Commander-in-Chief of the Four Directions, and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Dulu was made Duke of Grand Commandant and Commander-in-Chief of the Four Directions, and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 與尒朱兆入洛，兆還晉陽，留度律鎮京師。

translations.literal: He entered Luoyang with Erzhu Zhao. Zhao returned to Jinyang and left Dulu to garrison the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Luoyang with Zhao. Zhao returned to Jinyang and left Dulu to garrison the capital.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時，為使持節、侍中、大將軍、太尉、兼尚書令、東北道大行臺，與仲遠出拒義旗。

translations.literal: During the Former Deposed Emperor's reign, he served as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand General, Grand Commandant, concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing, and Northeast Branch Secretariat, and went out with Zhongyuan to resist the righteous standard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor, he held the posts of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Grand General, Grand Commandant, and concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, and as head of the Northeast Branch Secretariat marched out with Zhongyuan to oppose the rebel banner.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王間之，與尒朱兆遂相疑貳，自敗而還。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi, Xianwu, learned of this, he and Erzhu Zhao became mutually suspicious and divided, and they defeated themselves and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu, learned of this, he and Zhao turned suspicious of each other and fell to quarreling, defeating themselves before they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 度律雖在軍戎，聚斂無厭，所至之處，為百姓患毒。

translations.literal: Although Dulu was on campaign, his extortion was insatiable; wherever he went he was a plague upon the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Even on campaign Dulu extorted without limit. Wherever he went he was a scourge to the people.

sentences.zh: 其母山氏聞度律敗，遂恚憤而發病。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Shan, hearing that Dulu had been defeated, thereupon fell ill with rage and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Shan, hearing of Dulu's defeat, fell ill with grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 及度律至，母責之曰：「汝既荷國恩，無狀反叛，我何忍見他屠戮汝也。」

translations.literal: When Dulu arrived, his mother reproached him, saying: "You have received the state's grace, yet you shamelessly rebelled. How can I bear to see others slaughter you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Dulu arrived, his mother rebuked him, saying, "You owed the state a debt of gratitude, yet you rebelled without cause. How could I bear to watch others cut you down?"

sentences.zh: 言終而卒，時人怪異之。

translations.literal: When she finished speaking she died. People at the time marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: She died as soon as she had finished speaking. People at the time regarded it as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 後解大行臺，總隸長孫稚，戰於韓陵，敗還。

translations.literal: Later he was relieved of the Branch Secretariat and placed under Changsun Zhi's overall command. He fought at Hanling, was defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was later relieved of the Branch Secretariat and placed under Changsun Zhi's command. He fought at Hanling, was defeated, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿先據河梁，度律欲攻之，會大雨，晝夜不止，士馬疲頓，弓矢不得施用，遂西走於灅波津，為人擒執。

translations.literal: Helaba Chun first seized Heqiao. Dulu wished to attack him, but met with heavy rain that did not stop day or night. Troops and horses were exhausted, bows and arrows could not be used, and he thereupon fled west to Ruobo Ford, where men captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Helaba Chun had already seized Heqiao. Dulu tried to attack him, but a torrential rain fell without pause day and night. His men and horses were worn out, their bows useless, and he fled west to Ruobo Ford, where he was captured.

sentences.zh: 椿囚之，送於齊獻武王。

translations.literal: Chun imprisoned him and sent him to the Prince of Qi, Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Chun imprisoned him and sent him to Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 王送於洛，斬之都市。

translations.literal: The prince sent him to Luoyang and had him executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent him to Luoyang, where he was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 尒朱天光，榮從祖兄子。

translations.literal: Erzhu Tianguang was the son of Rong's father's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang was Rong's second cousin.

sentences.zh: 少勇決，善弓馬，榮親愛之，每有軍戎事要，常預謀策。

translations.literal: In youth he was brave and decisive, skilled with bow and horse. Rong loved him dearly, and whenever important military affairs arose, he was regularly included in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and resolute from youth, skilled in archery and horsemanship, he was a favorite of Rong's and was regularly consulted whenever important military matters arose.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，榮將擁眾南轉，與天光密議。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiaochang era, when Rong was about to lead his forces southward, he secretly discussed the matter with Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era, as Rong prepared to march south with his army, he consulted Tianguang in secret.

sentences.zh: 既據并肆，仍以天光為都將，總統肆州兵馬。

translations.literal: Once he had occupied Bing and Si, he still made Tianguang chief commander with overall command of Si Province's troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: After securing Bing and Si, he kept Tianguang as chief commander with overall authority over the troops and horses of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 肅宗崩，榮向京師，以天光攝行肆州，委以後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Rong went toward the capital and made Tianguang acting Governor of Si Province, entrusting him with rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Rong marched on the capital and left Tianguang as acting Governor of Si Province, entrusting him with affairs in the rear.

sentences.zh: 建義初，特除撫軍將軍、肆州刺史，長安縣開國公，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, he was specially appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, Governor of Si Province, and Duke of Chang'an County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era, he was specially appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Si Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Chang'an County with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 榮將討葛榮，留天光在州，鎮其根本。

translations.literal: When Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, he left Tianguang in the province to garrison the base region.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong set out against Ge Rong, he left Tianguang in the province to guard their base of power.

sentences.zh: 謂之曰：「我身不得至處，非汝無以稱我心。」

translations.literal: He said to him: "Where I myself cannot go in person, without you there is no one who can satisfy my heart."
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "Where I cannot go myself, no one but you can fulfill my intent."

sentences.zh: 永安中，加侍中、金紫光祿大夫、北秀容第一酋長。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era, he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, and First Chieftain of Northern Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he was further made Palace Attendant, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, and First Chieftain of Northern Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 尋轉衞將軍。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 大將軍元天穆東征邢杲，詔天光以本官為使持節、假鎮東將軍、都督，隸天穆，討破之。

translations.literal: Grand General Yuan Tianmu campaigned east against Xing Gao; an edict ordered Tianguang, with his existing office, to serve as Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the East, and Commander, subordinate to Tianmu, and he defeated Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Yuan Tianmu marched east against Xing Gao, an edict appointed Tianguang, retaining his existing rank, as Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the East, and Commander under Tianmu; he defeated Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，天光與天穆會榮於河內。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Tianguang and Tianmu joined Rong at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Tianguang and Tianmu rendezvoused with Rong at Henei.

sentences.zh: 榮發之後，并肆不安，詔天光以本官兼尚書僕射，為并肆雲恒朔燕蔚顯汾九州行臺，仍行并州，委以安靜之。

translations.literal: After Rong set out, Bing and Si were unsettled; an edict appointed Tianguang, with his existing office, also Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and head of the Branch Secretariat for the nine provinces of Bing, Si, Yun, Heng, Shuo, Yan, Wei, Xian, and Fen, while continuing as acting Governor of Bing Province, entrusting him with pacification.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong marched out, Bing and Si fell into unrest. An edict made Tianguang, at his existing rank, also Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and head of the Branch Secretariat for Bing, Si, Yun, Heng, Shuo, Yan, Wei, Xian, and Fen, while he continued as acting Governor of Bing Province and was charged with restoring order.

sentences.zh: 天光至并州，部分約勒，所在寧輯。

translations.literal: Tianguang reached Bing Province, organized and restrained the troops, and wherever he went order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang reached Bing Province, he deployed and disciplined the troops, and peace returned wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 顥破，尋還京師，遷驃騎將軍，加散騎常侍，改封廣宗郡公，增邑一千戶，仍為左衞將軍。

translations.literal: After Hao was defeated, he soon returned to the capital, was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, given the additional rank of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, had his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Guangzong Commandery with a fief increased by one thousand households, and remained General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao's defeat he soon returned to the capital, was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, had his title changed to Duke of Guangzong Commandery with a fief increased by one thousand households, and remained General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 醜奴棄岐州走還安定，置柵於平亭。

translations.literal: Chounu abandoned Qi Province and fled back to Anding, setting up stockades at Pingting.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu abandoned Qi Province and fled back to Anding, where he set up stockades at Pingting.

sentences.zh: 天光發雍至岐，與岳合勢於汧渭之間，停軍牧馬，宣言遠近曰：「今時將熱，非可征討，待至秋涼，別量進止。」

translations.literal: Tianguang set out from Yong and reached Qi, joined forces with He Yue between the Qian and Wei rivers, halted the army to graze horses, and proclaimed far and near: "The season is about to grow hot; campaigning is not feasible. Wait until autumn cools, and then decide anew whether to advance or halt."
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang marched from Yong to Qi, joined He Yue between the Qian and Wei rivers, halted to graze the horses, and proclaimed far and wide: "The heat is coming; this is no season for campaigning. Wait until autumn cools, and then we shall decide whether to advance or withdraw."

sentences.zh: 醜奴每遣窺覘，有執送者，天光寬而問之，仍便放遣。

translations.literal: Chounu frequently sent scouts; when any were seized and brought in, Tianguang treated them leniently, questioned them, and then released them.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu kept sending scouts. When any were captured and brought in, Tianguang questioned them gently and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 免者傳其待秋之言，醜奴謂以為實，分遣諸軍散營農稼，在岐州之北百里涇川。

translations.literal: Those who were released spread word of the plan to wait for autumn; Chounu took it for truth, dispersed his armies to camp separately and farm the fields, along the Jing River a hundred li north of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: The released men spread word that the army would wait for autumn. Chounu took this for truth, dispersed his forces to camp and farm along the Jing River a hundred li north of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 使其太尉侯伏侯元進領兵五千，據險立柵，且耕且守。

translations.literal: He had his Grand Commandant Houfuhou Yuanjin lead five thousand troops, seize strategic ground and erect stockades, both farming and defending.
translations.idiomatic: He put his Grand Commandant Houfuhou Yuanjin in command of five thousand men to hold the heights with stockades, farming while they defended.

sentences.zh: 在其左右，千人已下為一柵者，乃復數處。

translations.literal: To his left and right, in several places stockades were set up for units of one thousand men or fewer.
translations.idiomatic: On either flank, in several places, smaller stockades were set up for units of a thousand men or less.

sentences.zh: 天光知其勢分，遂密嚴備。

translations.literal: Tianguang knew their strength was divided and secretly made strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang saw that their strength was divided and secretly made ready for battle.

sentences.zh: 晡時，潛遣輕騎先行斷路，以防賊知，於後諸軍盡發。

translations.literal: In the late afternoon he secretly sent light cavalry ahead to cut the roads so the bandits would not learn of it; afterward all units set out together.
translations.idiomatic: In the late afternoon he secretly sent light cavalry ahead to block the roads and keep the bandits from learning of the move; then the whole army set out.

sentences.zh: 昧旦，攻圍元進大柵，拔之，諸所俘執，並皆放散，須臾之間，左右諸柵悉來歸款。

translations.literal: At daybreak he attacked and besieged Yuanjin's main stockade, took it, and released all captives taken; within moments the stockades left and right all came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he attacked and took Yuanjin's main stockade, released every captive, and within moments the stockades on both flanks surrendered.

sentences.zh: 前去涇州百八十里，通夜徑進，後日至城，賊涇州刺史侯幾長貴仍以城降。

translations.literal: A hundred eighty li short of Jing Province, they pressed forward through the night; on the second day they reached the city, and the bandits' Governor of Jing Province Houji Changgui surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred eighty li from Jing Province they pressed on through the night; on the second day they reached the city, and the rebel governor Houji Changgui surrendered it.

sentences.zh: [10]醜奴棄平亭而走，欲趨高平。

translations.literal: [10] Chounu abandoned Pingting and fled, intending to make for Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Chounu abandoned Pingting and fled toward Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 天光遣岳輕騎急追，明日，及醜奴於平涼長平坑，一戰擒之。

translations.literal: Tianguang sent He Yue with light cavalry in hot pursuit; the next day He Yue caught Chounu at Changping Ravine in Pingliang and captured him in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang sent He Yue with light cavalry in hot pursuit. The next day He Yue caught Chounu at Changping Ravine in Pingliang and captured him in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 天光明便共逼高平，城內執送蕭寶夤而降。

translations.literal: Tianguang marched swiftly to press on Gaoping together; within the city they seized Xiao Baoyin and delivered him in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang pressed swiftly on Gaoping. The city seized Xiao Baoyin and surrendered him.

sentences.zh: 賊行臺万俟道洛率眾六千人入山不下。

translations.literal: The bandits' Branch Secretariat attendant Wanqi Daoluo led six thousand men into the mountains and would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Branch Secretariat attendant Wanqi Daoluo led six thousand men into the mountains and refused to come down.

sentences.zh: 時高平大旱，天光以馬乏草，乃退於城東五十許里，息眾牧馬。

translations.literal: At the time Gaoping suffered severe drought; because the horses lacked forage, Tianguang withdrew some fifty li east of the city to rest the troops and graze the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping was then in severe drought. With the horses short of forage, Tianguang withdrew some fifty li east of the city to rest the men and graze the horses.

sentences.zh: 於是涇、豳、二夏，北至靈州，賊黨結聚之類，並來歸降。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Jing and Bin, the two Xia provinces, and north to Ling Province, bandit groups and those who had banded together all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, from Jing and Bin, the two Xia provinces, and north to Ling Province, rebel bands and armed groups all came to submit.

sentences.zh: 天光遣都督長孫邪利率二百人行原州事以鎮之。

translations.literal: Tianguang sent Commander-in-Chief Changsun Xieli with two hundred men to govern Yuan Province affairs and garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang sent Commander Changsun Xieli with two hundred men to administer Yuan Province and garrison it.

sentences.zh: 道洛招誘城人來掩，襲殺邪利并其所部。

translations.literal: Daoluo enticed men of the city to come in ambush and killed Xieli and his entire detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Daoluo incited men of the city to ambush and kill Xieli and his entire command.

sentences.zh: 天光與岳、悅等馳赴之，道洛出城拒戰，暫交便退，追殺千餘人，道洛還走入山，城復降附。

translations.literal: Tianguang rushed there with He Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others; Daoluo came out to fight, engaged briefly and withdrew; more than a thousand were killed in pursuit; Daoluo fled back into the mountains and the city submitted again.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang rushed there with He Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others. Daoluo came out to fight, exchanged a brief blow, and withdrew. More than a thousand were killed in pursuit. Daoluo fled back into the mountains, and the city submitted again.

sentences.zh: 天光遣慰喻，道洛不從，乃率眾西依牽屯山，據險自守。

translations.literal: Tianguang sent envoys to reassure him, but Daoluo would not obey; he then led his followers west to Qiantun Mountain and held the defiles.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang sent envoys to reassure him, but Daoluo refused. He then led his followers west to Qiantun Mountain and held the heights.

sentences.zh: 榮責天光失邪利，不獲道洛，復遣使杖之一百，詔降為散騎常侍、撫軍將軍、雍州刺史，削爵為侯。

translations.literal: Rong blamed Tianguang for losing Xieli and failing to capture Daoluo, again sent an envoy who beat him with the rod one hundred times, and an edict reduced him to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Yong Province, stripping his noble rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Rong blamed Tianguang for losing Xieli and failing to capture Daoluo, again sent an envoy to beat him with the rod one hundred times, and had him reduced by edict to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Yong Province, with his noble rank cut to marquis.

sentences.zh: 天光與岳、悅等復向牽屯討之。

translations.literal: Tianguang again marched against Qiantun with He Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang again marched against Qiantun with He Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others.

sentences.zh: 天光身討道洛，道洛戰敗，率數千騎而走，[11]追之不及，遂得入隴，投略陽賊帥王慶雲。

translations.literal: Tianguang personally pursued Daoluo; Daoluo was defeated in battle and fled with several thousand horsemen; [11] the pursuit could not overtake him, so he entered Long Province and threw himself on the bandit chieftain of Lüeyang, Wang Qingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang personally pursued Daoluo. Daoluo was defeated and fled with several thousand horsemen; [11] the pursuit could not catch him, so he entered Long Province and took refuge with the bandit chieftain of Lüeyang, Wang Qingyun.

sentences.zh: 慶雲以道洛驍果絕倫，得之甚喜，便謂大事可圖，乃自稱皇帝，以道洛為大將軍。

translations.literal: Qingyun thought Daoluo peerlessly fierce and resolute, and was greatly pleased to gain him; he believed the great enterprise could be achieved, declared himself emperor, and made Daoluo Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun considered Daoluo peerlessly fierce and was greatly pleased to gain him. He believed the great enterprise could be achieved, declared himself emperor, and made Daoluo Grand General.

sentences.zh: 天光欲討之，而莊帝頻敕，榮復有書，以隴中險邃，兼天盛暑，令待冬月。

translations.literal: Tianguang wished to attack them, but Emperor Xiaozhuang repeatedly issued edicts, and Rong also wrote, citing the deep peril of Long Province together with the sweltering summer heat, ordering him to wait until winter.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang wished to attack them, but Emperor Xiaozhuang repeatedly ordered otherwise, and Rong also wrote, citing the deep defiles of Long Province and the sweltering summer heat, telling him to wait until winter.

sentences.zh: 而天光知其可制，乃率諸軍入隴，至慶雲所居水洛城。

translations.literal: But Tianguang knew they could be subdued; he led the armies into Long Province and reached Shuiluo City where Qingyun resided.
translations.idiomatic: But Tianguang knew they could be subdued. He led the armies into Long Province and reached Shuiluo City, where Qingyun was encamped.

sentences.zh: [12]慶雲、道洛出城拒戰，天光復射中道洛臂，失弓還走。

translations.literal: [12] Qingyun and Daoluo came out to fight; Tianguang again shot Daoluo in the arm; he dropped his bow and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: [12] Qingyun and Daoluo came out to fight. Tianguang again shot Daoluo in the arm; Daoluo dropped his bow and fled.

sentences.zh: 破其東城，賊遂併趨西城，城中無水，眾聚熱渴。

translations.literal: They breached the eastern city; the bandits all rushed toward the western city; within the city there was no water and the masses sweltered with thirst.
translations.idiomatic: They breached the eastern city, and the rebels all crowded into the western city. With no water inside, the men sweltered with thirst.

sentences.zh: 有人走降，言慶雲、道洛欲突出死戰。

translations.literal: Someone came over in surrender and reported that Qingyun and Daoluo intended to break out in a desperate fight.
translations.idiomatic: Someone defected and reported that Qingyun and Daoluo meant to break out in a desperate fight.

sentences.zh: 天光恐失賊帥，燼釁未已，乃遣謂慶雲曰：「力屈如此，可以早降，若未敢決，當聽諸人今夜共議，明晨早報。」

translations.literal: Tianguang feared to lose the bandit leaders while embers of revolt had not yet died; he sent word to Qingyun: "Your strength is spent thus; you may surrender early. If you dare not decide, let your men consult together tonight and report early tomorrow morning."
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang feared to lose the rebel leaders while the embers of revolt still smoldered. He sent word to Qingyun: "Your strength is spent; you may surrender now. If you dare not decide, let your men consult tonight and report early tomorrow morning."

sentences.zh: 而慶雲等冀得小緩，待夜突出，報天光云，「請待明日」。

translations.literal: But Qingyun and the others hoped for a brief respite, planning a night breakout; they reported to Tianguang, "Please wait until tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: But Qingyun and the others hoped for a little breathing room, planning a night breakout. They replied to Tianguang, "Please wait until tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 天光因謂曰：「相知須水，今為小退，任取河飲。」

translations.literal: Tianguang therefore said, "Knowing you need water, I shall withdraw slightly for now; go take water from the river as you please."
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang therefore said, "Knowing you need water, I shall withdraw a little for now. Go take water from the river as you please."

sentences.zh: 賊眾安悅，無復走心。

translations.literal: The bandit troops were reassured and pleased, with no further thought of flight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel troops were reassured and lost all thought of flight.

sentences.zh: 天光密使軍人多作木槍，各長七尺，至黃昏時，布立人馬為防衞之勢，周匝立槍，要路加厚。

translations.literal: Tianguang secretly had the soldiers make many wooden spears, each seven chi long; at dusk he deployed men and horses in a defensive posture, setting spears all around with heavier ranks on the main roads.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang secretly had the soldiers make many wooden spears, each seven chi long. At dusk he deployed men and horses in a defensive line, set spears all around, and doubled them on the main roads.

sentences.zh: 又伏人槍中，備其衝突，兼令密縛長梯於城北。

translations.literal: He also hid men among the spears to guard against a breakout, and secretly had long ladders bound at the north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He also hid men among the spears to guard against a breakout, and secretly had long ladders prepared north of the city.

sentences.zh: 其夜，慶雲、道洛果便突出，馳馬先進，不覺至槍，馬各傷倒，伏兵便起，同時擒獲。

translations.literal: That night Qingyun and Daoluo indeed broke out, galloping ahead; before they knew it they reached the spears; horses were wounded and fell; hidden troops rose and captured them at once.
translations.idiomatic: That night Qingyun and Daoluo did break out, galloping ahead. Before they knew it they reached the spears; horses were wounded and fell; hidden troops rose and captured them at once.

sentences.zh: 餘眾皆出城南，遇槍而止。

translations.literal: The remaining troops all went out south of the city and halted upon meeting the spears.
translations.idiomatic: The rest went out south of the city and halted when they met the spears.

sentences.zh: 城北軍士登梯上城，賊徒路窮乞降，至明盡收其仗。

translations.literal: Soldiers north of the city mounted ladders and scaled the wall; the bandits, their escape cut off, begged to surrender; by daybreak all their weapons were collected.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers north of the city mounted ladders and scaled the wall. The rebels, with no way out, begged to surrender. By daybreak all their weapons had been collected.

sentences.zh: 天光、岳、悅等議悉坑之，死者萬七千人，分其家口。

translations.literal: Tianguang, He Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others debated burying them all alive; seventeen thousand died, and their households were distributed.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang, He Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others decided to bury them all alive. Seventeen thousand died, and their households were distributed.

sentences.zh: 於是三秦、河、渭、瓜、涼、鄯善咸來款順。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sanqin, He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shanshan all came to offer allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Sanqin, He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shanshan all came to submit.

sentences.zh: 天光頓軍略陽，詔復天光前官爵，尋加侍中、儀同三司，增邑至三千戶。

translations.literal: Tianguang encamped the army at Lüeyang; an edict restored Tianguang's former offices and titles; soon after he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant and Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and his fief was increased to three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang encamped at Lüeyang. An edict restored his former offices and titles, and soon after he was additionally made Palace Attendant and Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, with his fief increased to three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 秦州城民謀殺刺史駱超，超覺，走歸天光。

translations.literal: Men of Qin Province's capital plotted to kill Governor Luo Chao; Chao learned of it and fled to Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the Qin provincial capital plotted to kill Governor Luo Chao. Chao learned of it and fled to Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 天光復與岳、悅等討平之。

translations.literal: Tianguang again suppressed them with He Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang again put down the trouble with He Yue, Houmochen Yue, and the others.

sentences.zh: 南秦滑城人謀害刺史辛琛顯，[13]琛顯走赴天光。

translations.literal: Men of Huacheng in Southern Qin plotted to harm Governor Xin Chenxian; [13] Chenxian fled to Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Huacheng in Southern Qin plotted to harm Governor Xin Chenxian; [13] Chenxian fled to Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 天光遣師臨之，往皆克定。

translations.literal: Tianguang sent troops against them; wherever they went they pacified the trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang sent troops against them and pacified every place they reached.

sentences.zh: 初，賊帥夏州人宿勤明達降天光於平涼，後復北走，收聚部類謀為逆，攻降人叱干麒麟，欲并其眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, the bandit chieftain Suqin Mingda of Xia Province had surrendered to Tianguang at Pingliang; later he fled north again, gathered his tribesmen to plot rebellion, and attacked the surrendered Chigan Qilin, intending to absorb his following.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the bandit chieftain Suqin Mingda of Xia Province had surrendered to Tianguang at Pingliang. Later he fled north again, gathered his tribesmen to rebel, and attacked the surrendered Chigan Qilin, intending to absorb his following.

sentences.zh: 麒麟請救於天光，天光遣岳討之，未至，明達走於東夏。

translations.literal: Qilin begged Tianguang for rescue; Tianguang sent He Yue to attack him; before He Yue arrived Mingda fled to Eastern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin begged Tianguang for help. Tianguang sent He Yue against him, but before He Yue arrived Mingda fled to Eastern Xia.

sentences.zh: 岳聞榮死，故不追之，仍還涇州以待天光。

translations.literal: He Yue heard Rong had died, so he did not pursue further, but returned to Jing Province to await Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: He Yue heard that Rong had died, so he did not pursue further but returned to Jing Province to await Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 天光亦下隴，與岳圖入洛之策。

translations.literal: Tianguang also came down from Long Province and with He Yue plotted a strategy to enter Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang also came down from Long Province and with He Yue plotted a strategy to enter Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 進至雍州北，破叛已

translations.literal: He advanced to north of Yong Province; the rebels were already broken.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced north of Yong Province and had already defeated the rebels.

translations.literal: 〈Doubtful reading.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Doubtful reading.〉

sentences.zh: 詔遣侍中朱瑞詣天光慰喻。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Palace Attendant Zhu Rui to go to Tianguang with consolation and reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Palace Attendant Zhu Rui to Tianguang with words of consolation and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 天光與岳謀，欲令帝外奔，別更推立。

translations.literal: Tianguang plotted with He Yue, intending to have the emperor flee abroad and set up another claimant.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang plotted with He Yue to have the emperor flee abroad and set up another claimant.

sentences.zh: 乃頻啟云：「臣實無異心，惟仰奉天顏，以申宗門之罪。」

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized, saying: "Your subject truly has no other intent; I only look up to serve Your Majesty's countenance, to answer for my clan's guilt."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized: "Your subject truly has no other intent; I only look up to serve Your Majesty's countenance and answer for my clan's guilt."

sentences.zh: 又其下僚屬啟云：「天光密有異圖，願思勝算以防微意。」

translations.literal: Meanwhile his subordinate officials memorialized: "Tianguang secretly harbors divergent designs; may Your Majesty consider a winning stratagem to guard against incipient intent."
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile his subordinates memorialized: "Tianguang secretly harbors other designs. May Your Majesty consider a winning stratagem to guard against incipient intent."

sentences.zh: 既而莊帝進天光爵為廣宗王，元曄又以為隴西王。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Xiaozhuang promoted Tianguang's noble rank to Prince of Guangzong; Yuan Ye also made him Prince of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Xiaozhuang promoted Tianguang to Prince of Guangzong, and Yuan Ye also made him Prince of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 及聞尒朱兆已入京師，天光乃輕騎向都見世隆等，尋便還雍。

translations.literal: When he heard Erzhu Zhao had entered the capital, Tianguang rode lightly to the capital to see Shilong and the others, then soon returned to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Erzhu Zhao had entered the capital, Tianguang rode lightly to the capital to see Shilong and the others, then soon returned to Yong.

sentences.zh: 世隆等議廢元曄，更舉親賢，遣使告天光。

translations.literal: Shilong and the others debated deposing Yuan Ye and elevating someone close and worthy instead; they sent envoys to inform Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and the others debated deposing Yuan Ye and elevating someone close and worthy instead, and sent envoys to inform Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 天光與定策立前廢帝，又加開府儀同三司、兼尚書令、關西大行臺。

translations.literal: Tianguang joined in the decision to install the Former Deposed Emperor; he was further given the titles of Grandee with an Office Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Branch Secretariat of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang joined in the decision to install the Former Deposed Emperor and was further made Grandee with an Office Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, and head of the Grand Branch Secretariat of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 天光北出夏州，遣將討宿勤明達，擒之送洛。

translations.literal: Tianguang marched north from Xia Province and sent a general to attack Suqin Mingda; he was captured and sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang marched north from Xia Province, sent a general against Suqin Mingda, captured him, and sent him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時費也頭帥紇豆陵伊利、万俟受洛干等據有河西，[14]未有所附。

translations.literal: At the time the Feiyetou chieftains Hedouling Yili, Wanqi Shouluogan, and others held Hexi; [14] they had not yet attached themselves to any side.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Feiyetou chieftains Hedouling Yili, Wanqi Shouluogan, and others held Hexi; [14] they had not yet attached themselves to any side.

sentences.zh: 天光以齊獻武王起兵信都，內懷憂恐，不復北事伊利等，但微遣備之而已。

translations.literal: Tianguang, because Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu, had raised troops at Xindu, harbored inner anxiety and no longer campaigned north against Yili and the others, only sending slight forces to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu, had raised troops at Xindu, Tianguang was inwardly anxious and no longer campaigned north against Yili and the others, sending only light forces to guard against them.

sentences.zh: 又除大司馬。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 於時獻武王義軍轉盛，尒朱兆、仲遠等既經敗退，世隆累使徵天光，天光不從。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Huan's righteous army grew ever stronger; Erzhu Zhao, Zhongyuan, and the others having been defeated and driven back, Shilong repeatedly sent envoys summoning Tianguang, but Tianguang would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gao Huan's righteous army was growing ever stronger. Erzhu Zhao, Zhongyuan, and the others having been defeated and driven back, Shilong repeatedly summoned Tianguang, but Tianguang would not come.

sentences.zh: 後令斛斯椿苦要天光云：「非王無以能定，豈可坐看宗家之滅也。」

translations.literal: Later Helaba Chun urgently pressed Tianguang, saying: "Without Your Highness there is no one who can settle this; how can you sit by and watch the clan's destruction?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Helaba Chun urgently pressed Tianguang: "Without Your Highness there is no one who can settle this. How can you sit by and watch the clan's destruction?"

sentences.zh: 天光不得已而東下，與仲遠等敗於韓陵。

translations.literal: Compelled, Tianguang marched east and was defeated with Zhongyuan and the others at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: Compelled, Tianguang marched east and was defeated with Zhongyuan and the others at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿等先還，於河梁拒之。

translations.literal: Helaba Chun and the others had returned first and blocked him at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Helaba Chun and the others had returned first and blocked him at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 天光既不得渡，西北走，遇雨不可前進，乃執獲之，與度律送於獻武王。

translations.literal: Tianguang unable to cross, fled northwest; rain made advance impossible, and he was seized and captured; he and Dulu were sent to Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to cross, Tianguang fled northwest. Rain made further advance impossible, and he was captured. He and Dulu were sent to Gao Huan, Prince of Qi, Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 王致於洛，斬於都市，年三十七。

translations.literal: The prince had him taken to Luoyang and executed in the marketplace; he was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had him taken to Luoyang and executed in the marketplace. He was thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 尒朱專恣，分裂天下，各據一方。

translations.literal: The Erzhu clan acted wilfully, splitting the realm and each holding a region.
translations.idiomatic: The Erzhu clan acted wilfully, splitting the realm so that each held a region of his own.

sentences.zh: 天光有定關西之功，差不酷暴，比之兆與仲遠為不同矣。

translations.literal: Tianguang had the merit of pacifying Guanxi and was somewhat less cruel and violent; compared with Zhao and Zhongyuan he was not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang had the merit of pacifying Guanxi and was somewhat less cruel and violent; compared with Zhao and Zhongyuan he was a different man.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：尒朱兆之在晉陽，天光之據隴右，仲遠鎮捍東南，世隆專秉朝政，于時立君廢主易於弈棊，慶賞威刑咸出於己。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Erzhu Zhao at Jinyang, Tianguang holding Longyou, Zhongyuan guarding the southeast, Shilong monopolizing court governance—at the time enthroning or deposing rulers was as easy as moving pieces on a weiqi board; rewards, honors, authority, and punishments all issued from themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Erzhu Zhao at Jinyang, Tianguang holding Longyou, Zhongyuan guarding the southeast, Shilong monopolizing court governance—at the time enthroning or deposing rulers was as easy as moving pieces on a weiqi board; rewards, honors, authority, and punishments all issued from their own hands.

sentences.zh: 若使布德行義，憂公忘私，脣齒相依，同心協力，則磐石之固，未可圖也。

translations.literal: Had they spread virtue and righteousness, cared for the public and forgotten private interest, stood lip-to-teeth dependent on one another and joined hearts in common effort, then a foundation firm as bedrock could not have been assailed.
translations.idiomatic: Had they spread virtue and righteousness, cared for the public and forgotten private interest, stood lip-to-teeth with one another and joined in common effort, then a foundation firm as bedrock could not have been assailed.

sentences.zh: 然是庸才，志識無遠，所爭唯權勢，所好惟財色，譬諸溪壑，有甚豺狼，天下失望，人懷怨憤，遂令勁敵得容覘間，心腹內阻，形影外合。

translations.literal: Yet they were mediocre talents of no far vision; what they contended for was power alone, what they loved was wealth and women; like gullies and ravines, worse than jackals and wolves; the realm lost hope, men nursed resentment; thus powerful foes were given room to probe for openings—hearts divided within, while outwardly body and shadow united against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were mediocre men of no far vision. They contended for power alone and loved wealth and women. Like gullies and ravines, they were worse than jackals and wolves. The realm lost hope and men nursed resentment, until powerful foes were given room to probe for openings—hearts divided within while enemies without joined as body and shadow.

sentences.zh: 是以廣阿之役，葉落冰離；

translations.literal: Therefore at the battle of Guang'e, leaves fell and ice split apart;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at Guang'e, leaves fell and ice split apart;

sentences.zh: 韓陵之戰，土崩瓦解。

translations.literal: at the battle of Hanling, earth crumbled and foundations dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: at Hanling, earth crumbled and foundations dissolved.

sentences.zh: 一旦殄滅，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Wiped out in a moment—is this not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Wiped out in a moment—is this not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 傳稱「師克在和」，詩云「貪人敗類」，貪而不和，難以濟矣。

translations.literal: The Records say "An army conquers through harmony"; the Odes say "The greedy ruin their kind." Greedy and discordant, success was hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: The Records say, "An army conquers through harmony"; the Odes say, "The greedy ruin their kind." Greedy and discordant, they could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 元曄立 諸本「曄」作「暉」，北史卷四八尒朱榮附尒朱兆傳作「曄」。

translations.literal: On "Yuan Ye enthroned": in all editions Ye is written as Hui; Beishi juan 48, Erzhu Rong, appended Erzhu Zhao biography, has Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On "Yuan Ye enthroned": all editions write Ye as Hui; Beishi juan 48, Erzhu Rong, appended Erzhu Zhao biography, has Ye.

sentences.zh: 按尒朱世隆等立長廣王曄為帝，歷見本卷世隆傳、卷一０孝莊紀永安三年十月條、卷一九下南安王楨附元曄傳，「暉」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Per Erzhu Shilong and others elevating Prince of Changguang Ye as emperor, as repeatedly seen in this volume's Shilong biography, juan 10 Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang, 10th month of Yong'an year 3, and juan 19B Biography of Prince Nan'an Zhen, appended Yuan Ye biography—the character Hui is erroneous; corrected here accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong and others elevated Prince of Changguang Ye as emperor, as repeatedly seen in this volume's Shilong biography, juan 10 Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang, 10th month of Yong'an year 3, and juan 19B Biography of Prince Nan'an Zhen, appended Yuan Ye biography. The character Hui is erroneous; corrected here accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遂害帝於三級寺 諸本「三」作「五」，卷一０莊帝紀及通鑑卷一五四

translations.literal: On "They then killed the emperor at Sanji Temple": in all editions "three" is written "five"; juan 10 Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang and Zizhi Tongjian juan 154
translations.idiomatic: On "They then killed the emperor at Sanji Temple": all editions write "three" as "five"; juan 10 Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang and Zizhi Tongjian juan 154

sentences.zh: 〈四七九三頁〉
作「三」。

translations.literal: read "three."
translations.idiomatic: read "three."

sentences.zh: 按洛陽伽藍記卷一永寧寺條敍述此事也作「三級寺」。

translations.literal: Per the account in Luoyang qielan ji juan 1, Yongning Monastery entry, which also has "Sanji Temple."
translations.idiomatic: The account in Luoyang qielan ji juan 1, Yongning Monastery entry, also has "Sanji Temple."

sentences.zh: 本書卷一一二上靈徵志上稱永熙三年三月「并州三級寺南門災」。

translations.literal: This book's juan 112A Lingzheng zhi shang records, 3rd month of Yongxi year 3, "Fire at the south gate of Sanji Temple in Bing Province."
translations.idiomatic: This book's juan 112A Lingzheng zhi shang records that in the 3rd month of Yongxi year 3 there was "Fire at the south gate of Sanji Temple in Bing Province."

sentences.zh: 「五」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: The character "five" is erroneous; corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: The character "five" is erroneous; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 及張勸等掩襲世隆 北史卷六齊紀神武紀、卷四九斛斯椿傳，北齊書卷一神武紀

translations.literal: On "When Zhang Quan and others ambushed Shilong": Beishi juan 6 Qi Annals Shenwu ji, juan 49 Helaba Chun biography, Beiqishu juan 1 Shenwu ji
translations.idiomatic: On "When Zhang Quan and others ambushed Shilong": Beishi juan 6 Qi Annals Shenwu ji, juan 49 Helaba Chun biography, Beiqishu juan 1 Shenwu ji

translations.literal: 〈Supplied text.〉,
translations.idiomatic: 〈Supplied text.〉,

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一五五

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian juan 155
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian juan 155

sentences.zh: 〈四八二０頁〉
「張勸」作「張歡」。

translations.literal: "Zhang Quan" should read "Zhang Huan."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang Quan" is written here as "Zhang Huan."

sentences.zh: 按「張歡」又見北史卷一四后妃傳下周文皇后元氏傳，其人即北齊書卷二０、北史卷五三張瓊傳所記，「瓊子忻」。

translations.literal: According to the evidence, "Zhang Huan" also appears in Beishi juan 14, Biographies of Empresses and Consorts, under the biography of Empress Yuan of Emperor Wen of Zhou; that man is the person recorded in Beiqishu juan 20 and Beishi juan 53, Zhang Qiong biography, as "Qiong's son Xin."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang Huan" also appears in Beishi, juan 14, in the biography of Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wen of Zhou; he is the man recorded in Beiqishu, juan 20, and Beishi, juan 53, in the biography of Zhang Qiong, as Qiong's son Xin.

sentences.zh: 錢氏考異卷四０認為「齊史避諱，改『歡』為『忻』」。

translations.literal: Qian's Textual Variants, juan 40, holds that "the Qi history avoided the taboo and changed 'Huan' to 'Xin.'"
translations.idiomatic: Qian's Textual Variants, juan 40, argues that the Qi history avoided a taboo name and changed Huan to Xin.

sentences.zh: 此傳和下世隆傳的「張勸」當亦魏收避齊諱改，本名實是「歡」。

translations.literal: The "Zhang Quan" in this biography and in the later Shilong biography should likewise be Wei Shou's change to avoid a Qi taboo; the original name was in fact "Huan."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang Quan in this biography and in the Shilong biography that follows should also be Wei Shou's alteration to avoid a Northern Qi taboo; the man's real name was Huan.

sentences.zh: 顥既克滎陽擒行臺楊昱 百衲本「楊昱」作「陽叵」，他本都作「陽回」。

translations.literal: On "After Hao had taken Xingyang and captured Eastern Route Commissioner Yang Yu": in the patchwork edition "Yang Yu" is written "Yang E," while other editions all write "Yang Hui."
translations.idiomatic: On the passage where Hao took Xingyang and captured Eastern Route Commissioner Yang Yu: the patchwork edition reads Yang Yu as Yang E, while other editions read Yang Hui.

sentences.zh: 按卷一０孝莊紀永安二年五月丁巳記楊昱以東南道大都督鎮滎陽，乙丑又記「元顥陷滎陽，執楊昱」。

translations.literal: According to juan 10, Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang, on dingsi day in the fifth month of the second year of Yong'an, Yang Yu is recorded as Great Commander of the Southeastern Route garrisoning Xingyang; on yichou day it again records "Yuan Hao took Xingyang and seized Yang Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 10 of the Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang records that on dingsi day in the fifth month of Yong'an year 2, Yang Yu was stationed at Xingyang as Great Commander of the Southeastern Route, and on yichou day that Yuan Hao took Xingyang and captured Yang Yu.

sentences.zh: 其事亦見卷五八楊播附昱傳。

translations.literal: The event is also seen in juan 58, Yang Bo, appended biography of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The same event appears in juan 58, in the biography of Yang Yu, appended to the biography of Yang Bo.

sentences.zh: 雖「行臺」和「大都督」官稱有異，其時被元顥所擒的守滎陽的主將只有「楊昱」，「陽叵」或「陽回」都是「楊昱」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Although the titles "Eastern Route Commissioner" and "Great Commander" differ, the commander defending Xingyang who was then captured by Yuan Hao was only "Yang Yu"; both "Yang E" and "Yang Hui" are errors for "Yang Yu," and the text is corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Although the titles Eastern Route Commissioner and Great Commander differ, the only commander of Xingyang captured by Yuan Hao at that time was Yang Yu; Yang E and Yang Hui are both corrupt forms of Yang Yu, and the text is corrected here.

sentences.zh: 姦諂蛆酷多見信用 按「蛆」當作「狙」，意謂狡詐。

translations.literal: On "flatterers, worms, and the cruel were much trusted": according to the evidence, "worm" should be "macaque," meaning crafty and deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: On the phrase about flatterers and the cruel winning trust: the character read as "worm" should be "macaque," meaning cunning and treacherous.

sentences.zh: 忽有河內太守田怗家奴告省門亭長云 北史卷四八尒朱榮附世隆傳作「帖」，與「怗」通，冊府卷九五一

translations.literal: On "Suddenly a household slave of Tian Tie, Administrator of Henei, reported to the gate watchman of the Masters of Writing": Beishi juan 48, Erzhu Rong, appended Shilong biography, writes "Tie," interchangeable with "Tie," Cefu juan 951
translations.idiomatic: On the passage where a household slave of Tian Tie, Administrator of Henei, reported to the provincial gate watchman: Beishi, juan 48, appended biography of Shilong, writes the name as Tie, interchangeable with Tie; Cefu, juan 951

sentences.zh: 〈一一一八九頁〉
作「怙」。

translations.literal: writes "Hu."
translations.idiomatic: has Hu.

sentences.zh: 按卷八０賀拔勝傳見「田怙」。

translations.literal: According to juan 80, Helaba Sheng biography, "Tian Hu" appears.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 80, the biography of Helaba Sheng, records the name Tian Hu.

sentences.zh: 又北齊書卷二二李元忠附李愍傳說他曾奉命襲擊葛榮「所署廣州刺史田怙」。

translations.literal: Moreover, Beiqishu juan 22, Li Yuanzhong, appended biography of Li Min, says that he was once ordered to attack Ge Rong's "appointed Governor of Guang Province, Tian Hu."
translations.idiomatic: Beiqishu, juan 22, in the biography of Li Min appended to Li Yuanzhong, says he was once ordered to attack Ge Rong's appointed Governor of Guang Province, Tian Hu.

sentences.zh: 其人當即在此時叛降魏軍。

translations.literal: That man should be the one who at this time rebelled and surrendered to the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: That man is presumably the same person who defected to the Wei army at about this time.

sentences.zh: 「怗」疑是「怙」之訛。

translations.literal: "Tie" is suspected to be an error for "Hu."
translations.idiomatic: Tie is probably a corruption of Hu.

sentences.zh: 將車出東掖門 諸本「車」訛「軍」，今據北史卷四八、冊府

translations.literal: On "led the carriage out through the Eastern Side Gate": in all editions "carriage" is erroneously written "army"; the text is now corrected according to Beishi juan 48 and Cefu
translations.idiomatic: On the line about leading the carriage out through the Eastern Side Gate: all editions wrongly read carriage as army; the text is corrected from Beishi, juan 48, and Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same juan and page as above〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same fascicle and page as above〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: corrected.
translations.idiomatic: accordingly.

sentences.zh: 短小黑色 諸本脫「小」字，今據北史卷四八、冊府

translations.literal: On "short and black": all editions omit the character "short"; it is now supplied according to Beishi juan 48 and Cefu
translations.idiomatic: On the phrase short and black: all editions drop the word short; it is restored from Beishi, juan 48, and Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same juan and page as above〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same fascicle and page as above〉

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: supplied.
translations.idiomatic: restored.

sentences.zh: 復除軍州刺史 按地志無此州名，也不見紀傳，「軍」字當訛。

translations.literal: On "was again appointed Governor of Jun Province": according to the geographical monographs there is no such province, nor does it appear in annals or biographies; the character "Jun" must be erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: On his reappointment as Governor of Jun Province: no such province appears in the geographical treatises or in annals and biographies, so the character Jun must be corrupt.

sentences.zh: 賊涇州刺史侯幾長貴仍以城降 諸本「長貴」下旁注「疑」字。

translations.literal: On "the rebel Governor of Jing Province, Houji Changgui, thereupon surrendered the city": in all editions the note "doubtful" appears beside "Changgui."
translations.idiomatic: On the line where the rebel Governor of Jing Province, Houji Changgui, surrendered the city: all editions mark Changgui with a doubtful-reading note.

sentences.zh: 按周書卷一四賀拔岳傳也作「侯幾長貴」，並無可疑，今刪。

translations.literal: According to Zhoushu juan 14, He Yue biography, it also writes "Houji Changgui," and there is nothing doubtful; the note is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoushu, juan 14, He Yue's biography, also has Houji Changgui, with nothing doubtful about the name; the note is deleted.

sentences.zh: 率數千騎而走 諸本「率」訛「牽」，今據冊府卷四三二

translations.literal: On "led several thousand horsemen and fled": in all editions "led" is erroneously written "dragged"; the text is now corrected according to Cefu juan 432
translations.idiomatic: On the line about leading several thousand horsemen in flight: all editions wrongly read led as dragged; the text is corrected from Cefu, juan 432

sentences.zh: 〈五一四四頁〉
改。

translations.literal: corrected.
translations.idiomatic: accordingly.

sentences.zh: 至慶雲所居水洛城 諸本「水洛」作「永洛」。

translations.literal: On "reached Qingyun's seat at Shuiluo city": in all editions "Shuiluo" is written "Yongluo."
translations.idiomatic: On the line about reaching Qingyun at Shuiluo city: all editions read Shuiluo as Yongluo.

sentences.zh: 按卷一０孝莊紀

translations.literal: According to juan 10, Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang,
translations.idiomatic: Juan 10 of the Annals of Emperor Xiaozhuang,

sentences.zh: 〈三朝本〉

translations.literal: 〈Three-Dynasties edition〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Three-Dynasties edition〉

sentences.zh: 永安三年六月、周書卷一四賀拔岳傳、卷一七若干惠傳

translations.literal: sixth month of the third year of Yong'an, Zhoushu juan 14 He Yue biography, and juan 17 Gan Huibi biography
translations.idiomatic: the sixth month of Yong'an year 3, Zhoushu, juan 14, biography of He Yue, and juan 17, biography of Gan Huibi

sentences.zh: 〈百衲本〉

translations.literal: 〈patchwork edition〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈patchwork edition〉

sentences.zh: 作「水洛」。

translations.literal: write "Shuiluo."
translations.idiomatic: read Shuiluo.

sentences.zh: 今據改，參卷一０校記[一０]。

translations.literal: The text is now corrected accordingly; compare the collation note in juan 10, note [10].
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected accordingly; see the collation note in juan 10, note 10.

sentences.zh: 南秦滑城人謀害刺史辛琛顯 通鑑卷一五四

translations.literal: On "men of Huacheng in Southern Qin plotted to kill Governor Xin Chenxian": Zizhi Tongjian juan 154
translations.idiomatic: On the passage about men of Huacheng in Southern Qin plotting to kill Governor Xin Chenxian: Zizhi Tongjian, juan 154

sentences.zh: 〈四七七七頁〉
作「南秦州城民謀殺刺史辛顯」。

translations.literal: writes "the townspeople of Southern Qin Province plotted to kill Governor Xin Xian."
translations.idiomatic: reads, "the townspeople of Southern Qin Province plotted to kill Governor Xin Xian."

sentences.zh: 按南秦州之滑城不見紀載，疑「滑」字衍，通鑑「琛顯」作「顯」當是雙名單稱。

translations.literal: According to the evidence, Huacheng in Southern Qin Province is not recorded elsewhere; the character "Hua" is suspected to be an interpolation. In Zizhi Tongjian, "Chenxian" written as "Xian" should be the use of a single name from a double name.
translations.idiomatic: Huacheng in Southern Qin is not attested elsewhere, so Hua is probably an extra character. In Zizhi Tongjian, Chenxian rendered as Xian is presumably the familiar shortened form of a double given name.

sentences.zh: 万俟受洛干等據有河西 諸本及北史卷四八「干」作「于」。

translations.literal: On "Wanqi Shouluogan and others held the Hexi region": in all editions and Beishi juan 48, "gan" is written "yu."
translations.idiomatic: On Wanqi Shouluogan and others holding Hexi: all editions and Beishi, juan 48, write the final character of his name as yu rather than gan.

sentences.zh: 按北齊書卷二七万俟普傳

translations.literal: According to Beiqishu juan 27, Wanqi Pu biography,
translations.idiomatic: Beiqishu, juan 27, biography of Wanqi Pu,

translations.literal: 〈Supplied text.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Supplied text.〉

sentences.zh: 云：「子洛，字受洛干」，北史卷六齊紀一、北齊書卷二神武紀下並作「受洛干」。

translations.literal: It states: "His son Luo, style name Shouluogan"; Beishi juan 6 Qi Annals 1 and Beiqishu juan 2 Shenwu ji, part 2, both write "Shouluogan."
translations.idiomatic: It states that his son Luo had the style name Shouluogan; Beishi, juan 6, Qi Annals 1, and Beiqishu, juan 2, Shenwu ji, part 2, both have Shouluogan.

sentences.zh: 「于」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "yu" is erroneous; the text is now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu is corrupt and is corrected here.
